questions.stem: Which Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN solutions work together to define and enforce policies on the SD-WAN network? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Cisco's Catalyst Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) solutions include several components:

SD-WAN Manager is used for centralized visibility and management, including policy definitions.
SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart) implements and enforces the policies created in SD-WAN Manager.
SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond) performs tasks such as authentication, Network Address Translation (NAT) detection, and load balancing.
SD-WAN Analytics (formerly vAnalytics) is an optional analytics service.
SD-WAN Edge makes up the data plane and is responsible for forwarding traffic between locations via various media.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true of VRFs on a router?

options.text: All VRFs share a single routing table
A router will have more routing tables than VRFs
A VRF may use multiple routing tables
A router will have an equal number of VRFs and routing tables
A router will always have a single routing table

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A router will have more routing tables than VRFs

A router will have more routing tables than Virtual Router Functions (VRFs). This is because each VRF will have its own routing table, and a global routing table will exist for all traffic not flowing over a VRF.

The Cisco Secure Architectural Framework (SAFE) includes several secure domains for protecting Places in the Network (PINs), including:

Secure Services: Secure services are designed to protect insecure services and include Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), access controls, and encryption.
Management: Organizations should centrally manage devices and systems via consistent policy deployment, patching, and workflow change management. Policies, objects, and alerting fall under this domain.
Security Intelligence: Security intelligence provides insight into new and emerging threats and supports rapid and accurate threat detection.
Compliance: Compliance with regulations such as the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) and the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA).
Segmentation: Manual network segmentation uses addresses, Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs), and Access Control Lists (ACLs) to break the network into chunks. Cisco TrustSec uses identity-aware infrastructure to automatically perform software-defined segmentation and policy enforcement at scale.
Threat Defense: Threat defense monitors various data sources (network traffic, file reputation, etc.) to identify potentially suspicious activity and assess its associated risk and potential impacts on the organization.

Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs) could be used for various SAFE domains, such as Segmentation and Threat Defense, but aren't Secure Services solutions.

questions.stem: Order the events that occur during an HSRP implementation from initial configuration to normal operation.

options.text: Begin exchanging periodic Hello packets between group members to advertise priority values and detect the presence of peer routers on the segment

Forward all client traffic destined for the virtual gateway address through the Active router's physical interface, while the Standby router continues listening for Hellos in case a failover becomes necessary
Compare advertised priority values (or highest interface IP address as a tiebreaker) to determine which router transitions into the Active state for the group
Designate the router with the next-highest priority as Standby, positioning it to assume the Active role quickly if Hello packets from the Active router stop arriving
Configure HSRP group numbers, and assign a virtual IP address

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Configure HSRP group numbers, and assign a virtual IP address: Routers must first be placed in the same HSRP group and configured with a shared virtual gateway before any protocol operation can occur.
Begin exchanging periodic Hello packets between group members to advertise priority values and detect the presence of peer routers on the segment: Hello messages establish neighbor awareness and communicate the information needed for role selection.
Compare advertised priority values (or highest interface IP address as a tiebreaker) to determine which router transitions into the Active state for the group: HSRP elects the Active router based on configured priorities, using the highest IP address when priorities are equal.
Designate the router with the next-highest priority as Standby, positioning it to assume the Active role quickly if Hello packets from the Active router stop arriving: The Standby router continuously monitors the Active router and is prepared for rapid failover.
Forward all client traffic destined for the virtual gateway address through the Active router's physical interface, while the Standby router continues listening for Hellos in case a failover becomes necessary: In steady-state operation, the Active router forwards traffic for the virtual gateway while the Standby router remains ready to take over.

questions.stem: Which of the following commands is used to define which ACLs to use when creating a class for CoPP?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: class-map

In Control Plane Policing (CoPP), the class-map match-all class-map-name match access-group name acl-name is used to define classes based on Access Control Lists (ACLs).

ACLs can be created for classes using ip access-list command.

Policy maps are defined using the police command and specifying the conform, exceed, and violate actions (transmit or drop). Often, it’s best to set everything to transmit at first until baselines for normal traffic are established. Then, policies can be updated based on these baselines.

The service-policy {input|output} policy-name is used to apply a policy after it has been created.

ip access-group isn't used for CoPP.

questions.stem: Put the following steps in their recommended order to configure Cisco VTP version 3 across a switched network.

options.text: Configure each switch's VTP role according to its intended function within the topology
Set the VTP version to version 3 on each participating switch

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Set the VTP version to version 3 on each participating switch: You must globally enable VTP version 3 on the switches first, as the extended features and specific roles do not exist or parse correctly in the CLI under version 1 or 2.
Define the VTP domain name: Switches will not exchange database information or validate roles unless they belong to the same cryptographic or administrative domain boundary.
Configure each switch's VTP role according to its intended function within the topology: Before a switch can become operational, it must be designated as a server, client, or transparent node.
Designate a VTP primary server: Only the primary server is permitted to modify and propagate the VLAN database, protecting the network from unintended changes.

optionExplanations.A:
The source provides a shared explanation: Correct answer order:

questions.stem: Which of the following are common causes of issues with MST? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Two common problems with the Multiple Spanning Tree (MST) protocol include:

VLAN Assignment to the IST: If a VLAN is assigned to the Internal Spanning Tree (IST), then some ports associated with it might be unintentionally blocked. The IST works on all ports in a switch, so if there are two links between a pair of switches, one must be blocked in the IST (even if a VLAN is mapped to it). Assigning the VLAN to a different MST Instance (MSTI) fixes this.
Trunk Link Pruning: Pruning VLANs on trunk links aids in load balancing, but it can cause issues if VLANs in the same MST are present on different network links. When pruning trunk links, all VLANs in the same MSTI should be pruned.

MST doesn't require a primary switch to be specified.

The IST is created by default.

questions.stem:
The research department of a semiconductor development company needs full on‑premises control of all management components and cannot host any controllers in the cloud or allow external orchestration. A network architect suggests using Cisco Catalyst SD‑ WAN. 

Which response is appropriate for this recommendation?

options.text: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is not appropriate because it does not extend enterprise networks into the cloud.
Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is appropriate because it cannot enforce centralized device configuration and network management.
Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is not appropriate because it focuses on connecting remote branches.
Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is appropriate because all control plane functions are strictly handled by the local hardware switches.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is not appropriate because it focuses on connecting remote branches.

Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is designed primarily as a Wide Area Network ( WAN) solution to connect geographically dispersed locations. While it can be deployed on-premises, the solution often relies on orchestration components like SD-WAN Validator (previously vBond) and management through SD-WAN Manager, which are frequently hosted or require external connectivity for full functionality. So, in a specialized research environment that requires isolation and lacks a distributed branch structure, a traditional local area network or data center fabric is usually more appropriate.

Extending enterprise networks into the cloud is inappropriate for this scenario, in which the data should stay on-premises.

Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN does enforce centralized device configuration and network management, but that functionality is irrelevant to the scenario.

The control plane is centralized in the SD-WAN Controller (previously vSmart) rather than being distributed to individual site switches.

questions.stem: Order the following steps for automated implementation of Cisco SD-Access on top of a traditional campus network, from initial hardware requirements through full fabric operation.

options.text: Leverage Catalyst Center's Management Layer capabilities for ongoing automation, monitoring, and assurance across the fully operational SD-Access deployment
Implement the fabric policy plane, applying Security Group Tags (SGTs) via Cisco ISE integration to enforce segmentation and access policy across the fabric
Implement the fabric data plane, enabling VXLAN encapsulation, so traffic can be forwarded across the overlay using the control plane's mapping information
Implement the fabric control plane in which LISP is used to register and maintain a mapping database of endpoint identities and locations
Verify or install Physical Layer devices with the ASIC/FPGA hardware support required to perform VXLAN encapsulation and other fabric data-plane functions
Deploy and integrate Cisco Catalyst Center as the Controller Layer, establishing the platform that will provision and manage the fabric that follows
Establish a fully routed Layer 3 access underlay network, typically using IS-IS as the IGP, providing stable reachability between all fabric-capable devices

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Verify or install Physical Layer devices with the ASIC/FPGA hardware support required to perform VXLAN encapsulation and other fabric data-plane functions: Hardware must be physically capable before any software-defined capabilities can be introduced.
Deploy and integrate Cisco Catalyst Center as the Controller Layer, establishing the platform that will provision and manage the fabric that follows: Catalyst Center is typically installed early because it automates subsequent deployment activities.
Establish a fully routed Layer 3 access underlay network, typically using IS-IS as the IGP, providing stable reachability between all fabric-capable devices: Once Catalyst Center is live, it utilizes LAN Automation to programmatically deploy a loop-free Layer 3 routed underlay network, ensuring all loopback interfaces can communicate.
Implement the fabric control plane in which LISP is used to register and maintain a mapping database of endpoint identities and locations: With IP connectivity established, the LISP control plane is initialized to serve as the centralized tracking database that decouples endpoint identity from physical location.
Implement the fabric data plane, enabling VXLAN encapsulation, so traffic can be forwarded across the overlay using the control plane's mapping information: The data plane is laid over the control plane architecture, and VXLAN is enabled to map and wrap the actual transit packets in the data plane based on LISP lookup operations.
Implement the fabric policy plane, applying Security Group Tags (SGTs) via Cisco ISE integration to enforce segmentation and access policy across the fabric: Once the data plane can move traffic, the policy layer binds inline Scalable Group Tags (SGTs) into the VXLAN group policy option headers to enforce macro and micro-segmentation.
Leverage Catalyst Center's Management Layer capabilities for ongoing automation, monitoring, and assurance across the fully operational SD-Access deployment: After deployment, Catalyst Center continues providing lifecycle management and assurance services.

questions.stem: Which statement about PIM in bidirectional mode is accurate?

options.text: Only the RP participates in multicast routing.
Receiver hosts must join a group at an RP.
The IP address of the RP allows all routers to establish a loop-free spanning tree topology.
Sources must register with the RP to get their multicast traffic to flow down the shared tree.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The IP address of the RP allows all routers to establish a loop-free spanning tree topology.

In bidirectional PIM, the address of the rendezvous point ( RP) serves as a common root for a shared tree that allows traffic to flow in both directions. Every router in the network uses the unicast routing table to reach this address, which naturally creates a loop-free path back to the root.

Bidirectional PIM eliminates the registration process to allow data to flow directly up the tree.

Hosts join groups at their local designated router rather than interacting with the RP directly.

Every router along the path between the source and the receiver must participate in the multicast forwarding process.

questions.stem: The edge devices deployed in Cisco's Catalyst SD-WAN network comprise which plane?

Cisco’s Catalyst Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) solution implements various planes. SD-WAN Edge devices make up the data plane and are responsible for forwarding traffic between locations via various media.

Cisco’s SD-WAN Manager Network Management System ( NMS) and SD-WAN Validator (previously vBond) implement the management and orchestration planes respectively.

The policy plane is part of Cisco's Catalyst SD-Access.

Puppet Bolt can be used at scale, even though Puppet excels at continuous configuration enforcement.

Puppet Bolt uses SSH and WinRM rather than network configuration protocols.

VRFs are commonly used to allow overlapping address spaces on the same device.

questions.stem: A new switch has just joined a VTP domain. Which of the following messages will be sent?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Client requests

The Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) Trunking Protocol (VTP) uses three types of multicast advertisements, including:

Summary: Reports the VTP version, domain, configuration revision number, and timestamp. Sent every 300 seconds or when a change occurs.
Subset: Provides information about a change to the VLANs in the VTP domain and includes all information needed to make the change on a switch.
Client Requests: Clients can request a subset advertisement if, for example, they’ve just joined the VTP domain and the latest summary message has a higher configuration revision number than their latest version.

Update is not a VTP message type.

questions.stem: A router believes that part of its LSDB might be stale. Which of the following OSPF packets should it send out?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: LSR

The Open Shortest Path First ( OSPF) protocol includes five types of network packets:

Hello: Hello packets are sent out regularly to discover new OSPF neighbors and ensure that adjacent neighbors are still online.
Database Description (DBD or DDP): Packets exchanged when forming an OSPF adjacency that summarizes the contents of a router’s Link State Database ( LSDB).
Link-State Request (LSR): A router can use this packet to request a database download from a neighbor if it thinks part of its LSDB is out of date.
Link-State Update (LSU): Typically a response to an LSR, this contains database updates sent over a network link.
Link-State Ack: Acknowledgement flooded out in response to a flooded Link-State Advertisement (LSA).

questions.stem: According to Cisco's SAFE framework, which domain is used to establish boundaries for data and users?
questions.explanation:

The management domain is responsible for the orchestration, configuration, and monitoring of security policies across the network rather than the logical division of the network itself.

Security intelligence focuses on the collection and analysis of data to identify and react to threats.

Secure services provides specific security capabilities such as firewalls, IPS, and malware protection that are deployed within segments, but it does not define them.

questions.stem: In YANG, which of the following types of nodes emulates a database by storing a collection of records?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: List

The Yet Another Next Generation (YANG) data model language defines four types of nodes:

Leaf Node: Leaf nodes contain a single value of a particular type and have no children.
Leaf-List Node: Leaf-list nodes are sequences of leaf nodes with a single value of a particular type for each leaf node.
Container Node: Container nodes collect multiple related nodes into a subtree. Container nodes have child nodes but no value and contain an unlimited number of child nodes of any type.
List Node: List nodes hold a series of list entries, which act as records and are identified by their key leaves. A list node can have multiple keys and an unlimited number of child nodes of any type.

questions.stem: Which of the following STP states allows a port to send/receive BDPUs but not forward traffic or change the MAC address table?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Listening

In 802.1D Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), a switch port can be in the following states:

Disabled: Turned off.
Blocking: Port is turned on but doesn’t forward traffic to protect against loops. Receives Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs) but doesn’t send or change the Media Access Control (MAC) address table.
Listening: Next state after blocking where port can send and receive BPDUs but can’t forward network traffic or modify the MAC address table. Duration depends on STP forwarding time.
Learning: Can modify the MAC address table based on received traffic but still can’t forward traffic. Duration depends on STP forwarding time.
Forward: Port can now forward traffic and can perform any updates to MAC address table.
Broken: Port has a configuration or operational issue and discards packets until this is corrected.

optionExplanations.A:

In 802.1D Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), a switch port can be in the following states:

questions.stem: What does a type 2 hypervisor do?

options.text: Multiple operating systems running on a host operating system
Direct hardware access without an operating system

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Multiple operating systems running on a host operating system

A type 2 hypervisor, also known as a hosted hypervisor, is an application that is installed and runs on top of a pre-existing host operating system. The hypervisor relies on the host OS to manage hardware resources like the CPU, memory, and networking.

Applications using shared libraries describes a function of a standard operating system's dynamic linker or a containerization engine.

Direct hardware access without an operating system describes a type 1 (bare-metal) hypervisor.

Kernel level process isolation is a characteristic of containers that share the host's kernel but isolate processes.

questions.stem: Which type of Cisco IOS XE password stores password information in plaintext?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Type 0

Cisco IOS XE offers support for five types of passwords, including:

Type 0: Stored in plaintext in the device configuration without encryption or hashing. The enable password command uses a type 0 password. It is insecure.
Type 7: Use a Cisco-proprietary version of the insecure Vigenere cipher, which is easily decrypted. Enabled by the command service password-encryption for commands that would otherwise use type 0 passwords ( enable password, username password, and line password). It is insecure.
Type 5: Performs password hashing and salting using MD5, which is an insecure and easily crackable algorithm. It is insecure.
Type 8: Use the Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2 ( PBKDF2), a Secure Hash Algorithm ( SHA-256) hashed secret and password salting. Secure and recommended.
Type 9: Use the scrypt hashing algorithm and password salting. Secure, recommended, and preferred by Cisco.

questions.stem: Which of the following is responsible for forwarding traffic between locations in Cisco's Catalyst SD-WAN?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: SD-WAN Edge

Cisco’s Catalyst Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) solution implements various planes, including the control and data planes. The control plane is implemented using SD-WAN Controller (previously vSmart), which is responsible for defining the network topology and advertising routes and data policies to SD-WAN Edge devices. These SD-WAN Edge devices make up the data plane and are responsible for forwarding traffic between locations via various media.

Cisco’s SD-WAN Manager Network Management System (NMS) and SD-WAN Validator (previously vBond) implement the management and orchestration planes respectively.

questions.stem: Which term has the same meaning as NAT overload?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: PAT

Port Address Translation (PAT) is also referred to as NAT overload. In this configuration, the router translates multiple private IP addresses to a single public IP address and, to distinguish between the different traffic flows, the router uses unique TCP or UDP port numbers. 

Pooled NAT refers to Dynamic NAT, where the router has a list of public addresses and maps an internal host to one of the available public addresses in the pool, usually on a 1-to-1 basis until the pool is empty.

Dynamic NAT does not "overload" a single address with multiple hosts; it simply assigns a public address to a private host for the duration of its session.

Overlapping NAT occurs when internal and external networks use the same IP address space and requires specific translation techniques to resolve the conflict but is not synonymous with overloading.

SMI is used with SNMP for defining MIB objects rather than NETCONF data models.

JSON is a data encoding format, not a data modeling language used by NETCONF.

MIB represents a managed object database used by SNMP, not NETCONF.

questions.stem: Which command will enable recording user login and logout events when using TACACS+?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: aaa accounting exec

The aaa accounting exec command is used to track the start and stop times of user sessions on the device CLI. When paired with TACACS+, these events are sent to the TACACS+ server for auditing and tracking, providing visibility into who accessed the device and when sessions started and end.

The aaa authorization console command is used to enable authorization for the physical console port rather than recording session login and logout events.

The aaa authentication login command defines the methods used to verify a user identity during the initial login process but does not handle the auditing of the session itself.

The aaa new-model command enables the AAA framework but does not configure any accounting behavior.

questions.stem: Which of the following components of Flexible NetFlow define what type of data to collect? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Flexible NetFlow defines several types of components. The four types include:

Flow Records: Include key and non-key fields. Combination of default and user-configured records. The match command selects key fields, and the collect command selects non-key fields. The combination of key and non-key fields specifies what data to collect.
Flow Samplers: Samples NetFlow data rather than analyzing all of it (with a tradeoff between resource utilization and accuracy). Specify what to collect like Flow Records do but don't collect everything.
Flow Monitors: Applied to a particular interface to monitor traffic.
Flow Exporters: Exports data from Flow Monitor cache in NetFlow Version 9 to a remote system.

questions.stem: Which types of information can be found in an adjacency table? (Choose two.)

This allows the router or switch to forward packets efficiently without consulting the routing table for every packet.

Adjacency tables track the outgoing path, not the incoming interface.

Routing protocol metrics are part of the routing table, not the adjacency table used for forwarding.

questions.stem: Which of the following OSPF network packet types are used between two routers to update stale information in one's LSDB? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
The Open Shortest Path First ( OSPF) protocol includes five types of network packets:

Hello: Hello packets are sent out regularly to discover new OSPF neighbors and ensure that adjacent neighbors are still online.
Database Description (DBD or DDP): Packets exchanged when forming an OSPF adjacency that summarizes the contents of a router’s Link State Database (LSDB).
Link-State Request (LSR): A router can use this packet to request a database download from a neighbor if it thinks part of its LSDB is out of date.
Link-State Update (LSU): Typically a response to an LSR, this contains database updates sent over a network link.
Link-State Ack: Acknowledgement flooded out in response to a flooded Link State Advertisement (LSA).

questions.stem: Which of the following hypervisors needs to run on top of a client OS? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
A hypervisor is software that allows multiple Virtual Machines (VMs) to run on the same hardware. There are two types of hypervisors:

Type 1: A Type I, bare-metal, or native hypervisor runs directly on the device hardware with no Operating System (OS). Examples of Type 1 hypervisors include VMware vSphere, Citrix Hypervisor, and Red Hat Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM).
Type 2: Type 2 hypervisors are software that runs within a host operating system. VirtualBox and VMware Fusion are examples of Type 2 hypervisors, which are typically used by client machines.

questions.stem: Which plane is implemented by Cisco's SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart)?
questions.explanation:

Cisco’s Catalyst Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) solution implements various planes, including the control and data planes. The control plane is implemented using SD-WAN Controller, which is responsible for defining the network topology, advertising routes, and data policies for SD-WAN Edge devices.

These SD-WAN Edge devices make up the data plane and are responsible for forwarding traffic between locations via various media.

Cisco’s SD-WAN Manager Network Management System (NMS) and SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond) implement the management and orchestration planes respectively.

questions.stem: Order the following steps describing how TACACS+ provides Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) for network device access control.

options.text: The TACACS+ server validates the credentials and returns an authentication result to the device
The network device enforces the granted authorization level for the session and sends TACACS+ accounting records to document the user's session activity for auditing purposes
A user initiates a login attempt on the network device
The network device requests authorization from the TACACS+ server, which determines and returns the specific commands or privilege level the authenticated user is permitted to use
The network device, acting as the TACACS+ client, sends a separate authentication request containing the user's credentials to the configured TACACS+ server

A user initiates a login attempt on the network device: The Authentication, Authorization, and Accounting (AAA) process begins when a user attempts to access the device.
The network device, acting as the TACACS+ client, sends a separate authentication request containing the user's credentials to the configured TACACS+ server: The device forwards the authentication request to the TACACS+ server for credential validation.
The TACACS+ server validates the credentials and returns an authentication result to the device: Successful authentication confirms the user's identity before any privileges are granted.
The network device requests authorization from the TACACS+ server, which determines and returns the specific commands or privilege level the authenticated user is permitted to use: After identity is verified, the server determines what the user is authorized to do during the session.
The network device enforces the granted authorization level for the session and sends TACACS+ accounting records to document the user's session activity for auditing purposes: The device applies the authorized privileges while generating accounting records for auditing and compliance.

questions.stem: Which of the following protocols makes it possible to use TrustSec even if a switch along a packet's path doesn't support TrustSec?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: SXP

Cisco’s Security Group Tag (SGT) Exchange Protocol (SXP) is a peer-to-peer protocol for sending IP-to-SGT mappings from a “ speaker” to a “ listener” over one or more hops. It can be used to use TrustSec even if a switch along the patch lacks integrated TrustSec support.

MACsec Key Agreement (MKA) and the Security Association Protocol (SAP) are key management protocols for MACsec.

Media Access Control (MAC) Authentication Bypass (MAB) is an authentication mechanism.

questions.stem: Order the commands to configure BGP on a router using best practices.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

router bgp [as-number]: Enter BGP configuration mode, and define the local autonomous system.
bgp router-id [router-id]: Explicitly set the router ID used for BGP sessions and route origination rather than relying on automatic selection.
neighbor [ip-address] remote-as [as-number]: Define the BGP neighbor and its autonomous system number in global BGP configuration mode.
address-family [afi] [safi]: Enter the specific address-family submode (such as ipv4 unicast) in which per-address-family neighbor behavior will be configured.
neighbor [ip-address] activate: Explicitly activate the previously defined neighbor within this address-family, enabling route exchange for that specific address-family.

questions.stem: How should recommendations from Cisco Catalyst AI Assistant be handled in an enterprise?

options.text: By allowing AI to directly make configuration changes

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: By validating AI suggestions before implementation

A network engineer must always review AI recommendations to ensure they align with the specific security policies and business goals of the company. Validating the suggestions allows you to catch any potential errors or hallucinations before they can cause a disruption.

AI can sometimes make mistakes or provide general advice that does not fit a unique network environment perfectly, so following its advice exactly may not be ideal.

Giving an AI full control without a manual approval process creates a high risk of unintended network consequences.

Every change to a production network should be tested and verified, so AI changes should not be deployed without testing.

questions.stem: AES is the preferred algorithm option for which of the following IPsec protocols?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ESP

Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) is a set of protocols used for creating Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). Some key elements include:

Authentication Header (AH): The AH protects against replay attacks and ensures data integrity and peer authentication using digital signatures. It doesn’t provide data confidentiality via encryption. It has a protocol number of 51.
Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP): ESP provides data integrity, confidentiality, peer authentication, and replay protection. It has a protocol number of 50 and can carry packets either in tunnel mode (old packet’s headers are encrypted and new IPsec headers are added) or transport mode (only the original packet payload is encrypted). The Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) is the preferred algorithm for data encryption.
Internet Key Exchange (IKE): IKE performs mutual authentication and allows the creation of Security Associations (SAs), which are tunnels that carry data and control plane traffic for IPsec. Internet Key Exchange version two ( IKEv2) is the modern version of the protocol, which is more efficient, supports asymmetric authentication, and offers improved protocols and cryptographic algorithms.

IKE is a specific implementation of the Internet Security Association and Key Management Protocol (ISAKMP).

questions.stem: Which network tool gathers statistical information about traffic patterns?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: NetFlow

NetFlow collects detailed traffic flow statistics for analysis. It captures information about traffic patterns, such as source, destination, and usage, which can be used for monitoring, capacity planning, and security analysis.

Ping tests reachability, not traffic statistics.

Traceroute shows path hops, not traffic patterns.

SNMP gathers device metrics, not detailed flow statistics.

questions.stem: What are some requirements for neighbor adjacency when using OSPF? (Choose two.)

options.text: IP addresses must be in different subnets
OSPF hello and dead timers must match for the segment
RIDs must be unique between devices

questions.explanation:
Each OSPF router must have a unique Router ID (RID) to form and maintain neighbor relationships. Matching hello and dead timers are required so that routers agree on neighbor liveliness parameters. If these values do not match, OSPF neighbors will not progress past the INIT state.

OSPF typically attempts to avoid fragmentation by detecting the MTU, and a mismatch in MTU can actually prevent an adjacency from reaching the Full state.

OSPF neighbors must reside in the same IP subnet on a common network segment.

questions.stem: What happens when Cisco Express Forwarding (CEF) cannot handle a packet?

options.text: The packet is forwarded using fast switching.
The packet is queued until the FIB is rebuilt.
The packet is punted to the CPU.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The packet is punted to the CPU.

When a packet contains features or headers that are not supported by CEF, it is moved to the next level of switching logic. This process is known as punting, and it allows the main processor to handle complex tasks such as packets with IP options or those requiring fragmentation.

The router will make efforts to forward the traffic using a slower path before dropping the data.

Fast switching is a legacy architecture that is typically disabled when CEF is active on the device.

The Forwarding Information Base (FIB) is a prebuilt table, and packets are not held waiting for table updates during the forwarding process.

questions.stem: An OSPF area border router is transmitting LSAs between areas. Which type of LSA will be sent to the remote area?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Type 3

The Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) protocol uses six types of Link-State Advertisements (LSAs) to synchronize Link-State Databases (LSDBs) between routers for Internet Protocol version four (IPv4) networks, including:

Type 1 (Router LSA): Used to advertise LSAs originating within an OSPF area.
Type 2 (Network LSA): Used to advertise a Designated Router (DR)-attached multi-access network segment.
Type 3 (Summary LSA): Used to advertise network prefixes from a different OSPF area.
Type 4 (ASBR Summary LSA): Used to advertise a summary LSA for an Autonomous System Border Router (ASBR).
Type 5 (AS External LSA): Used to advertise LSAs for redistributed routes.
Type 7 (NSSA External LSA): Used to advertise redistributed routes in Not-So- Stubby Areas (NSSAs).

questions.stem: A BGP session on one of your routers is not coming up. You decide to check whether the neighbor is reachable. Which command would you use to perform this check?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: show tcp brief

The show tcp brief command displays the state of TCP connections, including those used by the Border Gateway Protocol (BGP). Since BGP relies on TCP port 179, this command can confirm that the session is established and whether a BGP neighbor is reachable at the TCP level.

The show running-config command only displays the configured BGP statements but does not indicate whether the session is currently established.

The show interfaces command is incorrect because it displays physical layer and data link layer statistics for a port rather than the status of an application-layer routing protocol session.

The show vtp status is incorrect because it is used to verify the configuration of the VLAN Trunking Protocol (VTP) and has no relevance to the BGP or TCP sessions.

questions.stem: Which term describes a sequence of entries that performs permit or deny actions?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Access control list

An access control list (ACL) is a sequential list of permit or deny statements. When a packet reaches an interface where an ACL is applied, the device looks at the first entry. If the packet matches, the action ( permit or deny) is taken immediately. If it does not match, it moves to the second entry, and so on.

Terminal lines are virtual ports ( VTY lines) used for management access, such as SSH.

AAA architecture is a broad framework for authentication, authorization, and accounting.

Control plane policing ( CoPP) is a specific application of filters used to protect the router's CPU rather than the name of the sequence of entries itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of NAT IP addresses must be reachable within an organization's network? (Choose two.)

Inside Local: Private IP address used by the device on the local network. Routable within the local network.
Outside Local: Apparent IP address of outside host from inside the local network. Considered a private IP address and must be reachable from within the local network.
Inside Global: Public IP address used by one or more inside local addresses on the outside network.
Outside Global: Public IP address assigned to an outside host on the outside network. Reachable on the outside network.

questions.stem:
An OSPF area contains routes for the following IP ranges:

192.168.1.0/24

192.168.2.0/24

192.168.3.0/24

An ABR has summarized this to 192.168.0.0/16. Which of the following IP ranges will be routed to the NULL0 interface? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
When implementing summarization, the Area Border Router (ABR) will create a discard route for the summarized range to the Null0 interface. Any addresses within the summarization range but outside of the specific ranges it summarized will match this route and be discarded.

The ranges that will be routed correctly include:

192.168.1.0/24

192.168.2.0/24

192.168.3.0/24

Since 192.168.0.0/24 and 192.168.4.0/24 fall outside these ranges, they will go to the NULL0 interface.

Both 192.168.1.0/24 and 192.168.3.0/32 are within the ranges and will be routed appropriately.

questions.stem: Which type of Cisco IOS XE password is recommended by Cisco and uses scrypt?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Type 9

Cisco IOS XE offers support for five types of passwords, including:

Type 0: Stored in plaintext in the device configuration without encryption or hashing. The enable password command uses a type 0 password and is insecure.
Type 7: Uses a Cisco-proprietary version of the insecure Vigenere cipher, which is easily decrypted. Enabled by the command service password-encryption for commands that would otherwise use type 0 passwords ( enable password, username password, and line password). It is insecure.
Type 5: Performs password hashing and salting using Message Digest 5 (MD5), which is an insecure and easily crackable algorithm. This is insecure.
Type 8: Use the Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2 (PBKDF2), a Secure Hash Algorithm (SHA-256) hashed secret and password salting. It is secure and recommended.
Type 9: Use the scrypt hashing algorithm and password salting. It is secure, recommended, and preferred by Cisco.

questions.stem: How is Port Address Translation (PAT) different from Pooled Network Address Translation (NAT)?

options.text: PAT provides a static one-to-one mapping of a local IP address to a global IP address.
PAT requires the use of a dedicated hardware appliance.
PAT uses a many-to-one mapping of many local IP addresses to one global IP address.
PAT uses a one-to-many mapping to assign multiple public IPs to a single local device.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: PAT uses a many-to-one mapping of many local IP addresses to one global IP address.

PAT is a specialized form of NAT that allows inside local devices to share a single inside global public IP address. It does this by assigning a unique source port number to every individual session. NAT provides a static one-to-one mapping of a local IP address to a global IP address.

PAT maps many local IPs to one global, not the reverse.

PAT is a software function on networking devices, so it does not need a dedicated hardware device.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the term for using MACsec between switches?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Uplink MACsec

Uplink MACsec encrypts traffic between switches and uses Cisco’s Security Association Protocol (SAP) encryption by default. Can be configured manually or dynamically using 802.1X authentication between the switches.

Downlink MACsec encrypts traffic between a switch and endpoint, uses the MACsec Key Agreement (MKA) protocol, and requires MACsec-capable supplicant on clients, such as Cisco Secure Client. Cisco switch can force encryption or non-encryption or make it optional. Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) can also provide an encryption policy with authorization results, which overrides local switch settings.

Ingress and egress MACsec are fabricated terms.

questions.stem: Cisco Talos is most relevant to which of the following secure domains of Cisco SAFE?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Security Intelligence

The Cisco Secure Architectural Framework (SAFE) includes several secure domains for protecting places in the network (PINs), including:

Security Intelligence: Security intelligence provides insight into new and emerging threats and supports rapid and accurate threat detection. Cisco Talos is Cisco's security research and threat intelligence team.
Segmentation: Manual network segmentation uses addresses, Virtual Local Area Networks ( VLANs), and Access Control Lists (ACLs) to break the network into chunks. Cisco TrustSec uses identity-aware infrastructure to automatically perform software-defined segmentation and policy enforcement at scale.
Management: Organizations should centrally manage devices and systems via consistent policy deployment, patching, and workflow change management. Policies, objects, and alerts fall under this domain.
Compliance: Compliance with regulations such as the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard ( PCI DSS) and Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act ( HIPAA).
Threat Defense: Threat defense monitors various data sources (network traffic, file reputation, etc.) to identify potentially suspicious activity and assess its associated risk and potential impacts on the organization.
Secure Services: Secure services are designed to protect insecure services and include Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), access controls, and encryption.

questions.stem: What does the switchport nonegotiate command accomplish?

options.text: It disables all trunking on the interface, preventing any tagged VLAN traffic from operating correctly
It prevents trunk ports from forming with dynamic desirable and dynamic auto switch ports
It blocks VTP advertisements through the interface, which prevents the switch from sharing or receiving any VLAN database updates
It stops all VLAN traffic from crossing the trunk and isolates any connected networks

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It prevents trunk ports from forming with dynamic desirable and dynamic auto switch ports

The switchport nonegotiate command disables the sending and receiving of Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP) frames on an interface. This prevents any dynamic trunk negotiation from occurring and is commonly used when trunking is manually configured or when connecting to non-Cisco devices.

This command only stops the negotiation protocol rather than the actual tagging of traffic, which continues as long as the port is in trunk mode.

The command does not impact the data plane or the ability of the switch to forward frames across a correctly configured link.

The command only affects the DTP and has no direct control over the VLAN Trunking Protocol (VTP).

A sandbox is a security mechanism for separating running programs to prevent them from affecting the rest of the system.

questions.stem: What do VTP transparent switches do?

options.text: Receive VTP messages without forwarding them or modifying VLANs in the VTP domain

Only process VTP messages if they come from a switch in the same VTP domain

Transparent switches forward VTP messages rather than blocking them.

Transparent switches process messages but ignore updates regardless of domain.

questions.stem: Which of the following rules apply to RIB logic for accepting or rejecting a route? (Choose two.)

options.text: If the AD of a new route is higher than one already present, the new route is rejected
Routes with a shorter prefix length are always preferred
If the new route does not already exist in the RIB, the new route is accepted
Metric values are evaluated before administrative distance

questions.explanation:
The Routing Information Base (RIB) acts as a centralized database that evaluates route offers from various sources. A higher AD represents a less trustworthy source; therefore, if a route with a lower AD (like a static route) is already present, a route with a higher AD (like OSPF) to the same destination will be rejected. When the RIB receives a route for a destination that is not currently in the table, it accepts it immediately.

In the RIB, routes with different prefix lengths are considered different destinations and can coexist.

Metrics are only used to compare routes within the same protocol.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an industry-standard alternative to a Cisco protocol that offers preemption by default and has a defined structure for VIP gateway MAC addresses?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: VRRP

First-Hop Redundancy Protocols (FHRP) help ensure network resiliency by creating a Virtual Internet Protocol ( VIP) gateway linked to multiple physical gateways. If a gateway goes down, then the devices’s traffic will be sent via another gateway. The three main FHRPs include:

Hot Standby Router Protocol ( HSRP): Protocol developed by Cisco that creates a virtual IP and Media Access Control (MAC) address usually held by the active router. If the active router fails, a standby router takes over these addresses and acts as the gateway.
Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP): Industry standard protocol that operates similarly to HSRP but names the routers “ master” and “ backup”. This protocol allows preemption by default and uses a particular MAC address structure for the VIP gateway.
Gateway Load Balancing Protocol ( GLBP): Offers both redundancy and load balancing. The network has up to four Active Virtual Forwarders (AVFs) responsible for forwarding traffic for their assigned hosts and a single Active Virtual Gateway (AVG) that responds to Address Resolution Protocol ( ARP) requests with the virtual MAC of the assigned AVF. Failure of the AVG or an AVF causes another system to take over its role.

NHRP is a fabricated term.

questions.stem: Which component of the Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN solution is responsible for advertising routes and data policies to edge devices?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: SD-WAN Controller

SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart) acts as the centralized brain of the SD-WAN solution by managing the control plane through the Overlay Management Protocol. It is responsible for distributing routing information security keys and data policies to edge devices across the fabric.

SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond) has the primary role of authenticating and authorizing edge devices during the initial joining process rather than advertising routes.

questions.stem: In 802.1D Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), all ports on the root bridge are which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Designated port

802.1D Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) has three port types:

Designated Port (DP): The Port receives and forwards Bridge Protocol Data Unit (BPDU) frames to other switches and provides downstream connectivity to devices and switches. Only one per link. All ports on the root bridge are designated ports.
Root Port (RP): Port connected to root bridge or upstream switch within a spanning tree; only one per switch.
Blocking Port: Port not forwarding traffic due to STP tree structure.

Alternate is not a port type in the original STP.

questions.stem: Given a router forwarding a packet out of a slow-speed WAN interface to a satellite-connected remote site, order the following delay components from smallest to largest contributor.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Processing delay: Modern routers typically process packets in hardware, making processing time the smallest contributor, usually on the order of microseconds.
Serialization delay: A slow-speed WAN interface requires measurable time to place all packet bits onto the wire, producing more delay than packet processing.
Propagation delay: Satellite links introduce enormous physical distances, making propagation delay by far the dominant contributor, typically hundreds of milliseconds.

questions.stem: In the Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP), which of the following combinations of switch port modes won't form a dynamic trunk?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Dynamic auto, dynamic auto

In the Dynamic Trunking Protocol (DTP), a switch port can be set to three different modes:

Trunk ( switchport mode trunk): The switch port is statically configured as a trunk port and uses DTP advertisements to try to establish a dynamic trunk with the other end.
Dynamic Desirable ( switchport mode dynamic desirable): By default the port acts as an access port, but it sends and listens for DTP advertisements to negotiate a dynamic trunk with the other end.
Dynamic Auto ( switchport mode dynamic auto): The default setting on Catalyst switches where the port only listens for DTP packets and will become a trunk if it receives them and negotiates successfully with the other end.

Two dynamic auto ports can't form a dynamic trunk with one another, but any other pair can.

questions.stem: Which of the following IGMP messages are sent by the server? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
The Internet Group Management Protocol version 2 ( IGMPv2) is common in multicast networks and is encapsulated in an Internet Protocol (IP) packet with an IP router alert set and a Time-To-Live (TTL) of 1. IGMP messages have five types:

Version 2 membership report (0x16): An IGMP join request used by a receiver to join a specified group or to answer a router’s membership query. This message states that a receiver still wants to receive messages from a group.
Version 1 membership report (0x12): Backward-compatible message to support IGMPv1.
Version 2 leave group (0x17): The receiver indicates that they want to leave the specified group.
General membership query (0x11): Sent by the server to an all-hosts group address (224.0.0.1) to check if the subnet contains any receivers. Uses a group address of 0.0.0.0. Each receiver will set random timers for each group and send a membership report for each assuming that they haven’t received a membership report for it from another receiver before the timer expires.
Group-specific query (0x11): Sent by the server to a group address after a receiver has asked to leave the group. Only sent if the receiver was the last one to respond to a general membership query. If no responses are received, then the router stops tracking and distributing that group’s messages.

questions.stem: Which of the following are examples of a Type 2 hypervisor? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
A hypervisor is software that allows multiple Virtual Machines (VMs) to run on the same hardware. There are two types of hypervisors:

Type 1: A Type I, bare-metal, or native hypervisor runs directly on the device hardware with no operating system. Examples of Type 1 hypervisors include VMware vSphere, Citrix Hypervisor, and Red Hat Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM).
Type 2: Type 2 hypervisors are software that runs within a host operating system. VirtualBox and VMware Fusion are examples of Type 2 hypervisors, which are typically used by client machines.

questions.stem: What does the term outside local mean in relation to NAT?

options.text: The public IP address assigned to a host on the outside network
The public IP address that represents one or more inside local IP addresses to the outside
The IP address of an outside host as it appears to the inside network
The private IP address assigned to a device on the inside network

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: The IP address of an outside host as it appears to the inside network

The outside local address is the IP address that your internal computers use to reach an external server. If you are using NAT to hide the real IP of an external server, you might map its real outside global address to a fake outside local address that fits into your internal IP scheme.

The private IP address assigned to a device on the inside network is an inside local address.

The public IP address that represents one or more inside local IP addresses to the outside is an inside global address.

The public IP address assigned to a host on the outside network is the outside global address, which is the real address of the host in the outside world.

questions.stem: What is the primary source of telemetry used by Cisco AI Endpoint Analytics?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: NBAR

Network-Based Application Recognition (NBAR) is the primary telemetry source because it performs deep packet inspection directly on the Catalyst 9000 series switches to identify device attributes. Data is sent to the Cisco Catalyst Center, where the AI engine uses it to assign the correct profiling labels to every device.

A configuration management database (CMDB) is an external source of truth used for enrichment rather than a primary source of live network telemetry.

SNMP is too simple to provide the deep application-layer details that the AI engine needs to accurately identify modern IoT devices.

While NetFlow provides very helpful flow data for behavioral analysis, it does not offer the same level of deep packet inspection as the NBAR feature.

questions.stem: What are some different ways to configure a username with password hashing on IOS XE? (Choose two.)

options.text: Using the command username (username) algorithm-type (sha256) secret (password)
Using the command username (username) encryption aes (password)

questions.explanation:
The standard username (name) secret (password) command uses a salted hash. For administrators requiring specific cryptographic standards, the algorithm-type keyword allows for the explicit selection of SHA-256, which provides a higher level of resistance against brute-force and rainbow table attacks. 

The command username (username) password (password) does not natively apply a strong cryptographic hash.

The command username (username) encryption aes (password) is incorrect because AES is a symmetric encryption algorithm typically used for data at rest or in transit but not a keyword used for local username hashing in IOS XE.

The sha256 and scrypt options are secure.

questions.stem: Which command enters IP SLA configuration mode on a router?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ip sla 1

The ip sla 1 command enters IP SLA configuration mode for operation number 1. From this mode, the administrator can define probes such as ICMP echo, UDP jitter, or TCP connect.

The do show ip sla configuration 1 command is an EXEC-level verification command and does not enter configuration mode.

The ip sla schedule 1 command is used to schedule an existing IP SLA operation rather than define it.

The ip sla responder command enables the responder feature but does not place the user into IP SLA operation configuration mode.

questions.stem: In the three-tier network model, which of the following layers is MOST likely to contain a wireless AP?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Access

The three-tier network design includes three layers:

Access Layer: Network edge where end-user devices (computers, Internet of Things ( IoT) devices, mobile, etc.) are connected to the network. This is the layer where wireless Access Points (APs) would be deployed.
Distribution Layer: A distribution layer switch connects to access-layer switches from a building, floor, etc. This layer creates a boundary between the access and core layers, creating a boundary for the Spanning Tree Protocol ( STP) and a summarization point for Internet Protocol (IP) routing information.
Core Layer: Connects multiple distribution-layer switches together to support multi-site networks. This includes physically distributed sites or corporate networks with data centers, cloud deployments, etc.

Edge is not a layer of the three-tier network model.

questions.stem: Which of the following IPsec protocols provide authentication, integrity protection, and defenses against replay attacks? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Internet Protocol Security (IPSec) is a set of protocols used for creating Virtual Private Networks (VPNs). Some key elements include:

Authentication Header (AH): The AH protects against replay attacks and ensures data integrity and peer authentication using digital signatures. It doesn’t provide data confidentiality via encryption. It has a protocol number of 51.
Encapsulating Security Payload (ESP): ESP provides data integrity, confidentiality, peer authentication, and replay protection. It has a protocol number of 50 and can carry packets either in tunnel mode (old packet’s headers are encrypted and new IPSec headers are added) or transport mode (only the original packet payload is encrypted).
Internet Key Exchange (IKE): IKE performs mutual authentication and allows the creation of Security Associations (SAs), which are tunnels that carry data and control plane traffic for IPsec. IKEv2 is the modern version of the protocol, which is more efficient, supports asymmetric authentication, and offers improved protocols and cryptographic algorithms.

IKE is a particular implementation of the Internet Security Association and Key Management Protocol ( ISAKMP).

Internet Key Exchange (IKE): IKE performs mutual authentication and allows the creation of Security Associations (SAs), which are tunnels that carry data and control plane traffic for IPsec. IKEv2 is the modern version of the protocol, which is more efficient, supports asymmetric authentication, and offers improved protocols and cryptographic algorithms.

IKE is a particular implementation of the Internet Security Association and Key Management Protocol ( ISAKMP).

questions.stem: Which scenarios are most likely to be resolved by using Cisco Catalyst Center (formerly Cisco DNA Center) Assurance Client 360? (Choose two.)

options.text: A user reports that video calls are often dropped when they roam among areas of the office.
A user reports that they have never been able to connect to a new company cloud app.
A user reports that their wired desktop keeps losing connectivity.
A user reports that their laptop connection was extremely slow earlier that day.

questions.explanation:
Cisco Catalyst Center Assurance Client 360 is a feature within Cisco's Catalyst Center platform that gives a complete view of wireless client devices on a network. It provides visibility into client roaming events, RF conditions, and mobility-related issues, making it suitable for diagnosing dropped video calls during movement. It also retains historical performance data, allowing administrators to investigate slow connections that occurred earlier in the day.

If the user connects to the network fine but cannot reach a specific app, the issue is probably a firewall rule, a DNS, a proxy, or the app itself, which Client 360 cannot diagnose.

Client 360 is focused on wireless clients, while a flapping connection on a wired desktop could be due to switch port errors, cable issues, or NIC problems.

questions.stem: Which of the following uses Cisco's Locator/ID Separation Protocol (LISP)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Control Plane

Cisco's Software Defined (SD)-Access includes three different planes:

Control Plane: Uses the Locator/ID Separation Protocol (LISP), which uses a central Map Server (MS) to track remote destination data, enabling routers to only manage local routes and ask the MS for remote routes.
Data Plane: Uses Virtual Extensible Local Area Network (VXLAN) to encapsulate traffic and perform tunneling while preserving the original Ethernet packet header. This enables the protocol to support overlays at Layers 2 and 3 and work on Internet Protocol (IP)-based networks that incorporate network segmentation and group-based policy.
Policy Plane: Uses Cisco TrustSec Scalable Group Tags (SGTs) to encode information about groups, and these tags are used to apply corporate policies.

Cisco SD-Access doesn't have a management plane.

questions.stem: Which steps are required to link object tracking to priority when using HSRP? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configuring the preferred device to lower its priority if the tracked object changes to a down state
Changing the preferred device’s priority to a higher value than other devices
Defining HSRP timers and poll intervals on all devices
Setting the virtual MAC address to match the tracked interface on the preferred device

questions.explanation:
HSRP elects the active router based on the highest priority, so the preferred device must be configured with a higher priority value. Object tracking allows HSRP to dynamically decrement that priority when a tracked object fails. This mechanism enables automatic role changes without manual intervention.

Defining HSRP timers and poll intervals affect hello and hold behavior, not priority tracking.

Virtual MAC addressing is independent of object tracking and priority logic.

The Destination EID is in the original IP header that is being carried inside the LISP tunnel; it is not a field within the shim header.

questions.stem: Which attribute in BGP is used for loop prevention?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: AS_PATH

AS_PATH is a well-known mandatory attribute that records every autonomous system (AS) number a route has passed through. Its primary job is loop prevention because when a BGP router receives a route update, it checks the AS_PATH list. If the router sees its own AS number already in that list, it knows the route has already visited its network and must be discarded to prevent a loop.

NEXT_HOP simply tells the router the IP address of the next hop to use to reach the destination.

LOCAL_PREF is a well-known discretionary attribute used for choosing the best path, not for preventing infinite loops.

Multi-exit discriminator ( MED) is used to influence how neighbors enter a network rather than preventing loops.

questions.stem: Which of the following Cisco IPsec VPN solutions support routing? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Route-based VPN solutions utilize virtual tunnel interfaces to treat the encrypted link as a logical point-to-point or multipoint interface. DMVPN uses multipoint GRE tunnels to support dynamic routing protocols like EIGRP and BGP. FlexVPN is built on the IKEv2 framework and utilizes virtual access interfaces to support dynamic routing and scalable topologies.

Traditional site-to-site IPsec VPNs use crypto maps and policy-based logic that do not natively support multicast or dynamic routing protocols without an additional GRE wrapper.

Remote-Access VPN is designed to connect individual clients to a gateway using specialized protocols that generally do not support the exchange of routing information between the client and the hub.

questions.stem: After replacing an access‑layer switch, you notice that VLANs across the domain suddenly disappear. Which setting on the newly replaced switch could be causing this issue?

options.text: It is running in VTP transparent mode
It has no VTP password configured
It has a higher configuration revision number
It has an incorrect VTP name

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It has a higher configuration revision number

In VLAN Trunking Protocol (VTP), the switch with the highest configuration revision number is considered authoritative. If a newly replaced switch has a higher revision number but an empty or incorrect VLAN database, it can overwrite VLAN information across the entire domain, resulting in VLANs disappearing network-wide.

A switch with a different VTP domain name will not participate in VTP updates at all.

Transparent mode does not advertise or apply VLAN changes to the domain.

Password mismatches block updates instead of overwriting VLANs.

questions.stem: Which of the following API security best practices protects against DoS attacks?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Rate Limiting

Some best practices for protecting RESTful Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) against attack include:

Implementing Strong Authentication and Authorization: APIs can use JSON Web Tokens (JWTs), OAuth, API keys, basic authentication, or other means. Authorization schemes include Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) or Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC).
Using HTTPS Encryption: HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure ( HTTPS) encryption protects API requests and responses against eavesdropping and modification by an attacker.
Rate Limiting and Throttling: Rate limiting and throttling protect against API abuse and Denial of Service (DoS) attacks by limiting the number of requests that a user can make.
Input Validation: Input validation protects against injection attacks. Methods include input validation, data sanitization, and output encoding.
Keeping APIs Updated: APIs may contain vulnerabilities that could be exploited by an attacker. Applying prompt updates helps to protect against this.

questions.stem: Which interface modes can be configured with the channel‑group command to form an LACP EtherChannel? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Configuring an EtherChannel requires selecting a mode that tells the switch which protocol to use and whether to actively seek a partnership with the neighboring device. For the industry-standard LACP, active forces the port into a state where it immediately begins sending negotiation frames, while passive puts the port into a listening state, waiting for the neighbor to start the conversation before participating in the bundle.

Auto is used to configure a port for the Cisco-proprietary PAgP in a passive listening state.

Desirable is used to configure a port for PAgP in an active negotiating state.

questions.stem: Which Cisco tool manages the network topology and advertises routes?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: SD-WAN Controller

Cisco’s Catalyst Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) solution implements various planes, including the control and data planes. The control plane is implemented using SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart), which is responsible for defining the network topology, advertising routes, and data policies for SD-WAN Edge devices.

SD-WAN Edge devices make up the data plane and are responsible for forwarding traffic between locations via various media.

Cisco’s SD-WAN Manager Network Management System (NMS) and SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond) implement the management and orchestration planes respectively.

vSphere is a VMware hypervisor.

Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN is a separate solution focused on WAN connectivity rather than campus fabric networking.

Cisco ISE integrates with SD-Access for identity and policy but is not a core architectural component.

questions.stem: A switch wants to send multicast messages only to those interfaces subscribed to a particular group. Which of the following solutions can help with this? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
By default, a switch will treat multicast Media Access Control (MAC) addresses as unknown multicast frames and flood them out on all ports but the one they received it from. The client is responsible for determining whether they care about the frame or want to discard it. Cisco switches offer two methods of reducing this flooding:

IGMP Snooping: The switch monitors Internet Group Management Protocol (IGMP) joins and tracks the interfaces associated with them. When it receives a frame for a group, it sends it out only on those interfaces that have joined that group.
Static MAC Address Entries: Multicast static entries can be programmed into a MAC address table, but this can’t respond to changes.

Network Address Translation (NAT) translates Internet Protocol (IP) addresses.

Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) sniffing is a fabricated term.

questions.stem: Which type of protocol solves the problem of hosts configuring multiple gateways by creating a Virtual IP (VIP) gateway?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: FHRP

First Hop Redundancy Protocols (FHRPs) solve the problem of default gateway redundancy by presenting hosts with a single Virtual IP (VIP) address. Multiple routers participate in the protocol, but only one forwards traffic while others are on standby, allowing hosts to configure one gateway while still achieving high availability.

Stateful SwitchOver (SSO) synchronizes control planes but does not provide a virtual gateway IP for hosts.

Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP) is a load-balancing FHRP variant, not the generic concept.

Equal-Cost Multi-Path (ECMP) provides multiple routing paths but does not create a virtual default gateway for hosts.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of routing protocols uses hop count as the sole metric for selecting a route?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Distance vector

Distance vector routing protocols use vectors to specify the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the next hop to reach the destination. The distance can be measured as hop count and is the metric for choosing a route.

Enhanced distance vector algorithms like the Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL) used by Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) can incorporate other metrics, such as bandwidth, reliability, delay, and load.

Link state algorithms like Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) and Intermediate System-to-Intermediate System (IS-IS) advertise link states and metrics for all connected links and directly-connected routers to the entire network. questions.stem: Order the following steps for DR/BDR election in OSPF on a multi-access network segment.

options.text: Each router compares the received priorities against its own and those of its neighbors to identify the highest-priority candidates among eligible routers (excluding any with priority 0)
Routers on the multi-access segment exchange Hello packets, each containing the sender's configured OSPF interface priority and RID
All remaining eligible routers become DROthers, forming full adjacencies only with the DR and BDR rather than with each other, reducing the total number of adjacencies on the segment
The router with the highest priority or, if tied, the highest RID is elected the DR
The router with the next-highest priority or, if tied, the next-highest RID is elected the BDR

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Routers on the multi-access segment exchange Hello packets, each containing the sender's configured OSPF interface priority and RID: Hello packets allow routers to discover neighbors and advertise the information used during the election.
Each router compares the received priorities against its own and those of its neighbors to identify the highest-priority candidates among eligible routers (excluding any with priority 0): Only routers with a priority greater than zero are eligible to become the DR or Backup Designated Router ( BDR).
The router with the highest priority or, if tied, the highest RID is elected the DR: The DR is selected using interface priority first and Router ID as the tiebreaker.
The router with the next-highest priority or, if tied, the next-highest RID is elected the BDR: The BDR is chosen to assume the DR role if the current DR fails.
All remaining eligible routers become DROthers, forming full adjacencies only with the DR and BDR rather than with each other, reducing the total number of adjacencies on the segment: This reduces the number of adjacencies from n(n−1)/2 to approximately 2n−3, improving scalability on broadcast networks.

questions.stem: How does the IntServ model of QoS function?

options.text: It automatically reroutes traffic to paths with the lowest total latency.
It lets applications signal the network to make bandwidth reservations.
It allows the network to identify classes that require special QoS treatment.
It limits the total number of users allowed on a link.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It lets applications signal the network to make bandwidth reservations.

Integrated Services relies on protocols like RSVP to allow applications to request and reserve bandwidth along a path. This ensures guaranteed service levels for specific traffic flows.

Allowing the network to identify classes that require special QoS treatment is DiffServ behavior.

IntServ does not perform dynamic path optimization.

IntServ manages resources per flow, not by limiting users.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not one of the three key components of path selection?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Hop count

Hop count is a metric used to choose paths in a distance vector routing algorithm.

Path selection chooses a path for a packet by looking at the Forwarding Information Base (FIB), which is programmed using the Routing Information Base (RIB), for the prefix length programmed there. Three key components of path selection include:

Prefix Length: The prefix length defines the range of Internet Protocol (IP) addresses that a path applies to, specified by the number of 1 bits in the subnet mask. The longer the prefix length (meaning the more specific the address), the more preferred the route.
Administrative Distance (AD): The AD defines how trustworthy the source of a route is. When choosing between equivalent routes (same prefix length) from different routing protocols, the AD is used to decide.
Metrics: Metrics are the basis for a routing protocol’s decision (path length, link state, etc.) and can vary from one algorithm to another.

questions.stem:
A new router has just been added to your network. Now, you want every interface on it to begin participating in OSPF without having to configure them one by one. 

Which command would you use to activate OSPF on all interfaces at once?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: network 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 area 0

The network 0.0.0.0 255.255.255.255 area 0 command matches all interface IP addresses on the router. This enables OSPF on every interface and assigns them to area 0, which is the fastest way to activate OSPF globally across all interfaces.

The router-id 0.0.0.0 command sets the OSPF router ID rather than enable OSPF on interfaces.

The passive-interface default command suppresses OSPF hellos rather than enable OSPF on interfaces.

The router ospf 1 command enters OSPF configuration mode but does not activate OSPF on any interface by itself.

questions.stem: Which of the following core claims in a JWT is used to define when a token is first valid?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: nbf

JSON Web Tokens (JWTs) encode a set of claims regarding a user that can be used to make access decisions. JWTs can use digital signatures (preferred) or Message Authentication Codes (MACs) to protect the integrity of the claims data. Core claims include iss (issuer), aud (audience), exp (expiration time), and nbf (not before time). The nbf claim specifies when a token first becomes valid.

questions.stem:
An engineer is interpreting an unfragmented packet capture on a transit underlay interface to analyze a software-defined network anomaly. 

Sequence the following protocol headers in the exact order they are encountered on the wire, processing from the outermost delivery transport boundary down to the raw payload.
questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Outer Ethernet Header: This is the immediate Layer 2 frame boundary used by underlay switches to forward the packet hop-by-hop between transit router interfaces.
Outer VXLAN IP Header: This is the underlay Layer 3 transport header containing the source and destination Virtual Extensible LAN Tunnel Endpoint (VTEP) IP addresses.
Outer VXLAN UDP Header: VXLAN encapsulates traffic inside UDP, utilizing a standard destination port of 4789 (or 4785 for Cisco SD-Access custom variations) to allow underlay load balancing via ECMP.
VXLAN Header: This is the specific 8-byte overlay metadata block that contains essential flags and the critical 24-bit VXLAN Network Identifier (VNI) used for fabric macro-segmentation.
Original Ethernet Header: Because VXLAN is a MAC-in-UDP overlay technology, the entire original inner Layer 2 frame header generated by the source endpoint is preserved here.
Original IP Header: This is the Layer 3 header containing the original source and destination IP addresses of the communication endpoints.
Data: The absolute innermost core of the packet containing the actual upper-layer protocol payload transmitted by the user application.
