questions.stem: Which of the following commands is used first when configuring a VLAN ACL?

options.text: match { ip address { acl-number | acl-name } | mac address acl-name }

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: vlan access-map name sequence

Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) Access Control Lists (VACLs) can filter traffic bridged in a VLAN or routed in or out of it. They are configured with the following commands:

vlan access-map name sequence: Defines a VLAN access map containing one or more map sequences, which include a match and an action statement.
match { ip address { acl-number | acl-name } | mac address acl-name }: Define a match statement for the traffic, using standard, extended, or named Internet Protocol version four (IPv4) ACLs or named Media Access Control (MAC) address ACLs.
action forward|drop [log]: Specify the action to be taken for matched traffic with optional logging for dropped traffic.
vlan filter vlan-access-map-name vlan-list. vlan-list: Apply the VACL to a single VLAN, VLAN range, or comma-separated list of VLANs.

questions.stem: You need to enable username-based authentication at login for a Cisco IOS XE device. Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: login local

The login local command tells the device to authenticate users against the local username database configured with the username command. This enables per-user authentication rather than using a single shared line password and is the standard method for enabling username-based login on console and VTY lines without external AAA servers.

The username <name> <password> command creates a user account rather than enabling authentication.

The authentication local command is not a standalone line configuration command in IOS XE.

The enable secret command controls privileged EXEC access rather than line login authentication.

questions.stem: What is the default timeout for NAT translations?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: 24 hours

By default, a Cisco router will keep a dynamic NAT translation in its table for 24 hours. However, when using Port Address Translation ( PAT), the individual entries will time out much faster to prevent the port numbers from being used up.

Ten minutes is closer to the default timeout for a UDP translation entry rather than the general NAT translation itself.

While one hour is a common interval for many network protocols, it is much shorter than the standard Cisco NAT default.

Three days would unnecessarily waste memory and public IP resources.

questions.stem: What are some differences between TACACS+ and RADIUS? (Choose two.)

options.text: TACACS+ can separate authentication, authorization, and accounting into independent functions
TACACS+ can provide secure network access control

questions.explanation:
TACACS+ treats authentication, authorization, and accounting as distinct processes, allowing granular control over each phase independently. questions.stem:
A network engineer is troubleshooting an intermittent WAN failover issue. They have configured the router to monitor a specific route, so it can switch to a backup path if the primary one disappears. 

To check if that route is currently up or down in real-time, which command should they use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: show track

The show track command displays the status of tracked objects, including specific routes configured for tracking. It indicates whether the tracked route is currently available or has failed.

The show ip route command only displays the routing table and the installed routes, not the real-time availability of a tracked route.

The traceroute command tests the path to a destination but does not monitor route availability in the routing table.

The ping command tests end-to-end reachability to a destination, not whether the route is being tracked in the routing table.

questions.stem: Which of the following commands can be used to configure OSPF? (Choose two.)

options.text: ip ospf process-id area area-id [secondaries none]

questions.explanation:
The Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) protocol can be configured in one of two ways:

OSPF Network Statement: The command network ip-address wildcard-mask area area-id enables OSPF on a router’s interfaces. The interfaces are advertised via a Link-State Advertisement (LSA) and added to the correct OSPF area within the OSPF Link-State Database (LSDB).
Interface-Specific Configuration: The command ip ospf process-id area area-id [ secondaries none] configures OSPF on a specific interface. Secondary connected networks are also added unless the secondaries none option is included. This approach is more targeted but less scalable.

The other two commands are fabricated.

questions.stem: Which syntax encases objects in JSON files?

Square brackets [] are used to define arrays, not objects.

Parenthesis () are not used anywhere in JSON syntax.

Colons : are only used to separate keys from values.

questions.stem:
A university campus with multiple interconnected buildings is struggling with growing traffic. They need to implement a network design that separates the core and distribution layers, and does so affordably. 

Which type of design should they use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: 3-tier

A 3-tier design separates the access, distribution, and core layers, which is ideal for large or growing campus networks. This architecture improves scalability, performance, and fault isolation across multiple interconnected buildings, while separating the core and distribution layers directly matches the university’s design requirement.

A 2-tier design collapses the core and distribution layers into a single layer rather than separating them.

A spine-leaf design is more expensive and optimized for data centers, not campus networks.

A hub-and-spoke design refers to a Wide Area Network (WAN) topology where remote sites connect to a central office.

questions.stem: In which of the following BGP neighbor states is a router waiting for a KEEPALIVE message to transition to the next state?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: OpenConfirm

The Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) defines six neighbor states, including:

Idle: Initial state of the BGP Finite State Machine (FSM), where the router sends Transport Control Protocol (TCP) connection requests and listens for connection requests from peers. If reentered due to error, resets ConnectRetryTimer to 60 and waits until it reaches 0 before trying again. Further failures cause the timer to double.
Connect: Router initiates the TCP three-way handshake. If successful, sends an Open message to a neighbor, resets ConnectRetryTimer, and transitions to OpenSent. If ConnectRetryTimer expires, attempts a new TCP connection and will transition to Active if the connection fails or Idle if other errors occur.
Active: Starts a new three-way TCP handshake. If successful, sends an Open message, sets hold timer to four minutes, and moves to OpenSent. If fails, reverts to Connect and resets ConnectRetryTimer.
OpenSent: Originating router waiting for an Open message from the receiving router. Once received, Open messages are checked for any errors. If no errors, hold time is negotiated, KEEPALIVE is sent, and moves to OpenConfirm. Errors cause a NOTIFICATION message and reversion to Idle state. TCP disconnect causes closed connection, reset ConnectRetryTimer, and move to Active. Other events cause reversion to Idle.
OpenConfirm: Router waits for KEEPALIVE or NOTIFICATION. If KEEPALIVE received, moves to Established. If an error occurs ( hold timer expiration, stop event, or received NOTIFICATION message), it reverts to Idle.
Established: BGP session established and neighbors exchange routes via UPDATE messages. UPDATEs and KEEPALIVES cause hold timer resets, and hold timer expiration causes error and reversion to Idle.

questions.stem: Which of the following involves buffering excess traffic which can help prevent it from being dropped? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Quality of Service (QoS) provides priority to certain types of network traffic, reducing latency, jitter, and packet loss for them. Common components of QoS include:

Classification and Marking: Dividing network traffic into classes based on its purpose and importance to the business. After traffic is classified, it is marked to allow QoS policies to be applied to it.
Policing: Policing helps to enforce traffic rates by transmitting or remarking inbound or outbound traffic that complies with the rates and dropping or marking down traffic that exceeds it.
Shaping: Shaping implements a buffer for egress traffic that holds traffic exceeding the traffic rate until the rate drops to the defined level. If traffic is below the desired traffic rate, then egress traffic isn’t buffered.
Congestion Management: Congestion management buffers excess traffic, and then removes packets from the queue via various algorithms.
Congestion Avoidance: Congestion avoidance attempts to proactively prevent network congestion by selectively dropping packets.

questions.stem: What issue prompted the creation of the Cisco Locator/ID Separation Protocol (LISP)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Routing scalability

LISP was created to address routing scalability problems caused by the rapid growth of routing tables in the global internet. By separating endpoint identity from location information, LISP reduces the size and churn of routing tables in the core.

LISP does not primarily focus on securing routing protocols or preventing attacks.

LISP does not directly provide redundancy or failover mechanisms.

LISP focuses on table size reduction, not faster convergence.

questions.stem: An organization has configured NAT to create a many-to-one relationship between inside and outside addresses. This describes which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: PAT

The three main types of Network Address Translation (NAT) include:

Static NAT: A private address has a static one-to-one mapping to a public address. Static NAT is further broken up into inside and outside static NAT.
Pooled NAT: Local Internet Protocol (IP) addresses are dynamically assigned one-to-one to a public address, which returns to the pool after a period of disuse.
Port Address Translation (PAT): Many local IP addresses are mapped to a single public IP address. Each internal IP/port combination in use is mapped to a different port on the public IP address.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately describe Virtual Tunnel EndPoints (VTEPs)? (Choose two.)

options.text: VTEPs have a local LAN interface and IP interface

VTEPs map Layer 2 and Layer 3 packets to the VNI to be used in the overlay network

The purpose of a VTEP is to encapsulate data within IP packets to traverse a Layer 3 underlay.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not a valid JSON object?
What are the three types of VTP advertisements?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Summary, subset, client requests

The three types of advertisements are summary, subset, and client request. Summary advertisements are sent every five minutes or whenever a change occurs to inform adjacent switches of the current VTP domain name and revision number. Subset advertisements follow a summary advertisement and contain the specific VLAN information such as names and IDs when a configuration change is detected. Client requests are generated by a switch when it detects that it has an older configuration revision number and needs the more current database from a server.

Trunk, dynamic desirable, and dynamic auto are different modes for the Dynamic Trunking Protocol.

Configuration, update, and acknowledgment are general networking terms that do not represent specific terms in VTP.

Client, server, and transparent describe the VTP modes that a switch can operate in rather than the advertisements it sends.

questions.stem: Which of the following are layers in the three-tier network model? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation:
The three-tier network design includes three layers:

Access Layer: Network edge where end-user devices (computers, Internet of Things (IoT) devices, mobile, etc.) are connected to the network.
Distribution Layer: A distribution layer switch connects to access-layer switches from a building, floor, etc. This layer creates a boundary between the access and core layers, creating a boundary for the Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) and a summarization point for Internet Protocol (IP) routing information.
Core Layer: Connects multiple distribution-layer switches together to support multi-site networks. This includes physically distributed sites or corporate networks with data centers, cloud deployments, etc.

Edge and management are not part of the three-tier model.

questions.stem: Order the following steps describing how the Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond Orchestrator) assists a WAN Edge device in detecting that it is operating behind a NAT device.

options.text: The WAN Edge device, situated behind a NAT device, sends a STUN request toward the Validator as part of its initial connection attempt
The Validator communicates the device's publicly translated address and port back to the WAN Edge device
The Validator receives the request and examines the source IP address and port exactly as they appear after translation by the intermediate NAT device
The WAN Edge device incorporates this translated address into its advertised TLOC information, allowing remote sites to establish tunnels using its correct public-facing address
The Validator compares this externally visible address/port against the address/port originally reported by the device itself, identifying a mismatch that indicates NAT is present

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

The WAN Edge device, situated behind a NAT device, sends a STUN request toward the Validator as part of its initial connection attempt: The WAN Edge device actively injects an initial request toward the public orchestration target to test the path.
The Validator receives the request and examines the source IP address and port exactly as they appear after translation by the intermediate NAT device: As the packet crosses the perimeter, the NAT device alters the headers and the Validator intercepts this modified payload to inspect the mutated Layer 3 and Layer 4 source properties.
The Validator compares this externally visible address/port against the address/port originally reported by the device itself, identifying a mismatch that indicates NAT is present: The Validator contrasts what the packet looks like on the wire with the internal private values documented inside the device payload to confirm a boundary translation occurred.
The Validator communicates the device's publicly translated address and port back to the WAN Edge device: Following identification, the Validator reflects the verified public reflection coordinates back down the pipe to inform the isolated edge device of its external persona.
The WAN Edge device incorporates this translated address into its advertised TLOC information, allowing remote sites to establish tunnels using its correct public-facing address: The edge device binds these public attributes to its Transport Locator ( TLOC), ensuring upstream OMP advertisements reflect the precise parameters required for peer fabrics to mount IPsec tunnels.

questions.stem: Which VXLAN control plane is used the most in campus environments?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: LISP control plane

In campus environments, VXLAN commonly uses the LISP control plane as part of Cisco SD-Access. LISP provides endpoint-to-location mapping that scales well for dynamic campus endpoints and simplifies mobility and policy enforcement across the campus fabric.

MP-BGP EVPN control plane is primarily used in data center VXLAN deployments, not campus fabrics.

Static unicast VXLAN tunnels do not scale and are not practical for large campus environments.

Multicast underlay is a method for handling broadcast, unknown unicast, and multicast traffic in the underlay but is not a full-featured control plane.

questions.stem: You are at the terminal of a router and need to check the stratum of its system clock. Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: show ntp status

This command is the primary tool used to see if a router or switch is synchronized. It provides the stratum level, which indicates the distance from the reference clock.

The show ntp peers command displays the stratum of the remote servers your device is talking to, but it does not explicitly show the current local status and final stratum of your own system's clock.

The show clock command only shows the current time and date stored in the software clock.

The show ntp associations command focuses on the relationship and reachability of external time sources rather than the summarized status of the local system.

questions.stem: Which statement accurately describes SSHv2?

options.text: It completely replaces the use of Telnet.
It sends data unencrypted over a network.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: It completely replaces the use of Telnet.

In a modern, professional network, SSHv2 is the industry standard for remote management because it provides strong encryption for both the login credentials and the entire data session. While Telnet was used for decades, it sends everything in plaintext, meaning anyone on the path can read the data.

The entire purpose of SSH is to provide a secure, encrypted connection.

SSHv2 is a completely separate protocol from SSHv1, with a different internal architecture.

SSHv2 requires a reliable, connection-oriented session to handle the encryption handshake and data delivery, so it uses TCP port 22 rather than UDP.

questions.stem: Which of the following are non-key fields that can be used with the collect command to create customized flow records? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
In a Flexible NetFlow configuration, the collect command is used to add non-key fields to a flow record to provide additional context without changing how the router identifies a unique stream of traffic. IP source AS is a non-key attribute that provides autonomous system information for traffic analysis without affecting flow uniqueness. Interface output can be collected to indicate the egress interface used by the flow.

IP ToS is a key field to differentiate flows based on service class.

Source port numbers are part of the core key fields used to uniquely identify flows.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions can be used as part of Cisco SAFE for threat prevention? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
The Cisco Secure Architectural Framework (SAFE) is designed to address threats at all stages of the attack lifecycle, including:

Before: Establishing policies and implementing preventative security measures, such as Cisco Secure Firewalls, identity services, and Network Access Control (NAC).
During: Performing threat detection, analysis, and incident response. Uses tools such as Next-Generation Intrusion Prevention Systems (NGIPS), Next-Generation Firewalls (NGFWs), malware protection, and email and web security solutions to identify, block, and protect against active threats.
After: Detecting, containing, and remediating an attack and implementing lessons learned for the future. Uses tools such as Cisco Advanced Malware Protection (AMP), NGFWs, and Cisco Network Analytics.

questions.stem: Which of the following Cisco endpoint security solutions can be used to verify that endpoints follow corporate policies about the use of antivirus before allowing them on the network?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Cisco Secure Client

Endpoint security involves protecting devices against potential threats. Cisco offers many solutions and services designed to implement endpoint security in a campus environment, including:

Cisco Secure Client: Formerly Cisco AnyConnect Secure Mobility Client, this provides a Virtual Private Network (VPN) and can verify that an endpoint complies with corporate policies regarding the use of antivirus, antispyware, and firewall software before granting network access.
Cisco Talos: Talos is Cisco’s security research team that generates threat intelligence used by Cisco products.
Cisco Secure Malware Analytics: Formerly ThreatGrid, Cisco Secure Malware Analytics performs static and dynamic malware analysis within a sandboxed environment, comparing it to millions of samples. It also performs behavioral analytics and uses threat intelligence to determine the purpose of the malware and its potential impacts.
Cisco Advanced Malware Protection (AMP): Cisco AMP provides malware protection throughout the attack lifecycle by identifying inbound malware using threat intelligence and Secure Malware Analytics, detecting active malware using file reputation and sandbox analysis, and retrospective analysis to identify malware that has slipped through the cracks. AMP connects to many other Cisco security solutions.
Cisco Umbrella: Formerly OpenDNS, Cisco Umbrella blocks Domain Name System ( DNS) requests for known malicious domains, preventing malware from being downloaded from or communicating with malicious sites.
Cisco Secure Web Appliance: A web gateway that uses threat intelligence to block malware downloads and communication, visits to risky sites, data exfiltration, and other web-related threats.
Cisco Secure Email: Uses threat intelligence to block spam, forged emails, phishing attacks, malware, and data exfiltration via email.
Cisco Secure Intrusion Prevention System (IPS): Formerly FirePOWER NGIPS, this system monitors network traffic for potential attacks and blocks it. It also offers real-time contextual awareness, advanced threat protection and remediation, intelligent security automation, Application Visibility and Control (AVC), and URL filtering.

questions.stem: Which of the following code snippets is in correct JSON format?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: {"user": "root", "id": 1, "password": "rgq0L2nDYd7&YhYF"}

Correct JSON objects must be enclosed in curly braces and contain key-value pairs where the keys are always strings wrapped in double quotes. The values can be strings, numbers, or other valid data types, and each pair is separated from the next by a comma.

Angle brackets <> and tags are the primary structural components of XML rather than JSON.

JOSN objects require curly braces and quotes.

Square brackets [] are reserved for lists and arrays rather than for mapping specific keys to values.

questions.stem: A network engineer is configuring IPv4 access control on a Cisco router using the legacy access-list global configuration command. Which ACL types can be created using this command? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Numbered standard ACL: This is a correct selection because numbered standard ACLs are created using the access-list global configuration command. These ACLs use a numeric range, typically 1 through 99 and 1300 through 1999, and filter traffic based only on the source IPv4 address. This command represents the legacy method of ACL configuration and is still supported for backward compatibility and simpler deployments. Engineers often use this method for quick configurations without requiring named structures.

Numbered extended ACL: This is also a correct selection because numbered extended ACLs are created using the same access-list command. These ACLs use number ranges such as 100 through 199 and 2000 through 2699, and they provide more granular filtering by evaluating source and destination IP addresses, protocols, and ports. This makes them more flexible than standard ACLs. The access-list command allows engineers to define these rules directly in global configuration mode.

Named ACL: This is incorrect because named ACLs are created using the ip access-list command, not the access-list command. Named ACLs provide better readability and easier management, especially in large configurations, because they allow the use of descriptive names instead of numeric identifiers. They also support sequence numbers and easier editing, which are not features of numbered ACLs created with the access-list command.

Port ACL ( PACL): This is incorrect because PACLs are applied at Layer 2 switch ports and are not directly created using the access-list command as a distinct ACL type. Instead, PACLs typically reference standard or extended ACLs that were created using access-list or ip access-list commands. PACL describes the application of an ACL to a switch port, not a unique ACL type created by the command itself.

VLAN ACL ( VACL): This is incorrect because VLAN ACLs are not created using the access-list command. Instead, they are configured using the vlan access-map command and applied to VLANs. While VACLs can reference ACLs defined elsewhere, they are part of a different feature set used for filtering traffic within a VLAN rather than at Layer 3 interfaces.

questions.stem: Why are CoPP policies used?

options.text: To ensure that all traffic leaving the device is marked with the correct Quality of Service tags
To block network traffic based on the Application layer they are applicable to
To increase the overall switching throughput of the data plane interfaces for users
To limit traffic to the control plane CPU to a specific rate based on class

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: To limit traffic to the control plane CPU to a specific rate based on class

CoPP policies are designed to protect the control plane by rate-limiting traffic destined for the CPU based on traffic classes. This prevents excessive or malicious traffic from overwhelming the CPU and impacting routing, management, or control protocols and helps the device maintain stability under high load or attack conditions.

CoPP focuses on control plane protection rather than Application layer filtering.

CoPP does not optimize or accelerate data plane forwarding.

CoPP polices inbound control plane traffic, so it does not perform any QoS marking.

questions.stem: A port has portfast enabled. Which mode of the STP will it start with when turned on?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Forwarding

Portfast is a Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) feature that prevents hosts from generating Topology Change Notifications (TCNs) since they only have one connection to the network anyway. These access ports skip the learning and listening states in 802.1D STP and immediately can forward traffic.

In 802.1D STP, a switch port can be in the following states:

Disabled: Turned off
Blocking: Port is turned on but doesn’t forward traffic to protect against loops. Receives Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs) but doesn’t send or change the Media Access Control (MAC) address table.
Listening: Next state after blocking where port can send and receive BPDUs but can’t forward network traffic. Duration depends on STP forwarding time.
Learning: Can modify the MAC address table based on received traffic but still can’t forward traffic. Duration depends on STP forwarding time.
Forward: The Port can now forward traffic and can perform any updates to the MAC address table.
Broken: The Port has a configuration or operational issue and discards packets until this is corrected.

questions.stem: Which automation tool uses playbooks and plays?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Ansible

Ansible is an open-source automation engine that uses a simple, human-readable language called YAML. Its hierarchy is based on a sports metaphor: A playbook is the entire file that contains your automation strategy for a group of servers. Inside that playbook is one or more plays that map a specific set of hosts to a specific role.

Chef uses a cooking metaphor with configuration files called recipes, which are grouped into cookbooks.

SaltStack uses SLS files and pillars to manage its infrastructure rather than playbooks.

Puppet uses manifests and modules.

questions.stem: The concept of an Internal Spanning Tree (IST) is part of which of the following protocols?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: MST

The Multiple Spanning Tree protocol (MST) has an Internal Spanning Tree (IST) labeled instance 0 that applies to all ports and Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) on all switches in the MST region.

The Spanning Tree Protocol (STP), Rapid STP (RSTP), and Per-VLAN Spanning Tree Plus (PVST+) are other STPs that lack the concept of an IST.

questions.stem: Which of the default privilege levels in the Cisco IOS XE CLI is indicated by a hash sign (#) in the CLI?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: 15

The Cisco IOS XE CLI has three privilege levels by default:

Privilege Level 0: Only can use the disable, enable, exit, help, and logout commands.
Privilege Level 1 ( User EXEC): Indicated by a greater than sign (R1>) and doesn’t allow use of the configure terminal command for configuration changes.
Privilege Level 15 ( Privileged EXEC): Indicated by a hash sign (R1#) and allows full access to commands.

10 is not a default privilege level.

questions.stem: Which of the following is most commonly used to test the reachability of a remote host?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ping

The ping command is a built-in utility used to determine whether a remote system is reachable via the network. The default ping command (ping ip-address) sends five Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) packets and looks for responses from the remote system.

The traceroute command maps the route that a packet takes between a source and destination, including the Internet Protocol (IP) address or Domain Name System (DNS) name and latency of each hop along the way. By default, traceroute will try connecting 30 times before considering a destination unreachable.

Debugging provides deeper insight into what might be going wrong with protocols such as Open Shortest Path First (OSPF).

The Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) enables device configuration and management over the network.

questions.stem: What is IGMP snooping?

options.text: A protocol for blocking IGMP traffic
A method to reduce multicast flooding
A way to prioritize multicast packets over unicast packets
A technique that captures IGMP packets to search for sensitive information

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: A method to reduce multicast flooding

IGMP snooping allows a switch to listen to IGMP messages between hosts and multicast routers and keep a table of IGMP joins. By doing so, the switch forwards multicast traffic only to ports that have subscribed to a multicast group, preventing unnecessary flooding of multicast packets to all ports.

The term snooping in this context refers to traffic inspection for forwarding logic rather than malicious data collection.

Prioritization is handled by quality of service mechanisms rather than IGMP management.

The goal of this feature is to facilitate and optimize the delivery of multicast traffic rather than preventing it.

The exclamation point and equal sign (!=) are used to check if two values are not equal to each other.

The triple equal sign (===) is used in languages like JavaScript for strict equality, but it has no meaning in Python.

questions.stem:

Which command designates that interface for PAT?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ip nat outside

The ip nat outside command designates the router interface that connects to the external network. Without defining an outside interface, the router cannot properly perform PAT for outbound traffic.

The ip nat inside command configures the internal-facing interface, not the interface that performs PAT to the outside.

ip nat pool command is incorrect because it defines a range of public IP addresses for dynamic NAT, not the interface.

ip pat outside is not a valid IOS command.

questions.stem: What are some ways that PBR can route packets? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Policy-Based Routing (PBR) allows a network administrator to bypass the standard routing table to identify specific traffic and define its next-hop. PBR can use access lists to match specific protocol types, such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP, to determine the routing path. Like traditional routing, PBR can still be configured to match and route based on the destination IP address of the packet.

PBR operates on a per-packet basis rather than a per-session basis because it does not inherently track the state of a connection.

While Layer 2 switching uses MAC addresses, PBR is a Layer 3 function that relies on packet headers and does not typically use the source or destination MAC address for routing decisions.

questions.stem: Order the following 802.1p Class of Service traffic types from lowest to highest priority.

options.text: Video with < 100 ms latency and jitter
Voice with <10 ms latency and jitter

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Background: Background traffic has the lowest practical forwarding priority and yields to all higher-priority classes.
Best effort: Best-effort traffic receives the default forwarding treatment without preferential handling.
Excellent effort: Excellent effort receives slightly better treatment than best-effort traffic while remaining below business-critical applications.
Critical applications: Business-critical applications receive preferential forwarding ahead of normal data traffic.
Video with < 100 ms latency and jitter: Interactive video requires lower latency and jitter than ordinary application traffic.
Voice with <10 ms latency and jitter: Voice traffic receives very high priority because of its stringent delay and jitter requirements.
Internetwork control: Routing and other internetwork control protocols require very high priority to maintain network operation.
Network control: Network control traffic has the highest priority because it is essential for the operation and stability of the network infrastructure.

questions.stem: Which of the following fields shown as the result of the show ip neighbor ospf command are used during a DR/BDR election?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: PRI

PRI indicates the priority assigned to the Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) neighbor's interface. These priority values are used when electing a Designated Router (DR) or Backup DR (BDR).

The neighbor ID is the router's ID number, the address is its Internet Protocol (IP) address, and the interface indicates the local interface that the neighbor is attached to.

The state field describes the current neighbor state and whether the interface is a DR or BDR.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions is designed to protect against network loops introduced by adding an unauthorized switch to a network?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: BPDU guard

Bridge Protocol Data Unit (BPDU) guard places ports with portfast enabled into an ErrDisabled state if they receive a BPDU, rather than moving them to learning. This blocks the port from processing network traffic and is designed to protect against potential loops if a switch is added without authorization.

BDPU filter blocks a port from sending BPDUs. It’s enabled globally with spanning-tree portfast bpdufilter default and managed locally with spanning-tree bpdufilter enable.

Portfast is a Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) feature that prevents hosts from generating Topology Change Notifications (TCNs) since they only have one connection to the network anyway. These access ports skip the learning and listening states in 802.1D STP and immediately can forward traffic. If the port ever receives a BPDU, then portfast is disabled and it moves to the learning state.

Root guard prevents a port from becoming a root port in STP, which can prevent a downstream switch from accidentally becoming a root bridge. It causes the port to act like it’s in a listening state and can’t forward traffic when it receives superior BPDUs for any Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) on the port.

STP loop guard prevents alternative or root ports from becoming designated ports if the root port stops receiving BPDUs. The original root is placed in a loop inconsistent state while down and can recover and transition through STP states after the issue is fixed.

questions.stem: What are some performance advantages of using PCI passthrough? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
PCI passthrough is a virtualization technique that allows a guest virtual machine to have a direct, exclusive connection to a physical PCI device, such as a high-speed network interface card (NIC) or a graphics processing unit (GPU). Direct access to I/O resources is the main benefit because the VM can talk to the hardware at nearly native speeds without waiting for a virtual driver to translate the signals. Using a bypassed hypervisor strategy eliminates the overhead of managing shared access.

PCI passthrough actually decreases the CPU load on the host.

PCI passthrough can make it harder to move a VM to another server since the new server would need the same physical hardware card to be available.

questions.stem: How is ERSPAN different from RSPAN?

options.text: ERSPAN mirrors packets at the data plane level.
ERSPAN sends traffic to the local system through Layer 3.
ERSPAN requires a dedicated physical cable.
ERSPAN can be used for analyzing traffic.

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: ERSPAN sends traffic to the local system through Layer 3.

ERSPAN wraps copied data inside a Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE) header. Unlike RSPAN, which requires a dedicated Layer 2 VLAN to be stretched across all switches, ERSPAN uses a standard IP packet to carry the mirrored data, meaning the traffic can be routed across routers, firewalls, and WAN links.

SPAN, RSPAN, and ERSPAN all mirror packets at the data plane level and are used for analyzing traffic.

ERSPAN uses the existing IP infrastructure to move data.

questions.stem: Why would a large international business want to use Cisco Enterprise Network Functions Virtualization (ENFV)? (Choose two.)

questions.stem: How does Cisco AI Endpoint Analytics flag potentially risky endpoints?

options.text: By adding endpoints to a CMDB
By scanning endpoints for open ports

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: By assigning trust scores

Cisco AI Endpoint Analytics continuously monitors the behavior of every device and assigns a trust score based on how closely that behavior matches its known profile. The AI engine detects anomalies and lowers a device’s score to alert the administrator.

Adding endpoints to a CMDB can help profile a device, but adding it to the database is not how the AI flags it as risky.

Access control lists are used to block traffic rather than to detect risk itself.

Scanning endpoints for open ports is part of the overall security process, not the primary AI flagging mechanism.

questions.stem: A central Map Server (MS) is a critical component of which plane of Cisco SD-Access?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Control Plane

Cisco's Software-Defined Access (SD-Access) includes three different planes:

Control Plane: Uses the Locator/ID Separation Protocol (LISP), which uses a central Map Server (MS) to track remote destination data, enabling routers to only manage local routes and ask the MS for remote routes.
Data Plane: Uses Virtual Extensible Local Area Network (VXLAN) to encapsulate traffic and perform tunneling while preserving the original Ethernet packet header. This enables the protocol to support overlays at Layers 2 and 3 and work on Internet Protocol (IP)-based networks that incorporate network segmentation and group-based policy.
Policy Plane: Uses Cisco TrustSec Scalable Group Tags (SGTs) to encode information about groups, and these tags are used to apply corporate policies.

Management and orchestration are not valid planes for SD-Access.

optionExplanations.A:
Source explanation: Correct answer: Control Plane

Cisco's Software-Defined Access (SD-Access) includes three different planes:

questions.stem: Which actions can occur when BPDU filter is enabled globally and the switch receives a BPDU? (Choose two.)

options.text: The switch can process a BPDU sent from a superior switch
The switch can transmit a BPDU to inferior downstream switches
The switch can ignore a BPDU and continue to filter traffic
The switch can place a port into an ErrDisabled state

questions.explanation:
When BPDU filter is enabled globally, it suppresses BPDUs only on PortFast ports until a BPDU is received. Upon receiving a BPDU, the port immediately disables BPDU filtering and PortFast. The interface then participates fully in STP, including processing received BPDUs and transmitting BPDUs to downstream switches.

Placing the state into an ErrDisabled state is associated with BPDU guard, not BPDU filter.

Ignoring a BPDU and continuing to filter traffic occurs when BPDU filter is enabled directly on an interface.

Transparent modifies PTP packets by updating the correction field instead of simply passing them unchanged.

Boundary mode acts as a time source for downstream devices.

Grand server mode is the primary authoritative time source for the entire network, typically synced to a GPS or atomic clock.

questions.stem: Which issues can the debug ip ospf adj command help directly diagnose? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
debug ip ospf adj displays events related to Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) adjacency formation and maintenance. A maximum transmission unit (MTU) mismatch can prevent neighbors from advancing beyond the ExStart or Exchange state because Database Description packets advertise an interface MTU. The command can expose the adjacency negotiation failure and the conflicting MTU values.

On network types that require matching masks, an improperly configured network mask can prevent an OSPF adjacency from forming. Adjacency debugging can report this mismatch while the routers process neighbor information. This output helps distinguish a mask mismatch from other causes of failed adjacency formation.

Hello and dead interval mismatches are identified more directly with debug ip ospf hello or by comparing interface settings with show ip ospf interface. These timers must match between neighbors, but they are hello packet parameters rather than the primary focus of adjacency event debugging.

An unreachable remote host is an end-to-end connectivity symptom and does not by itself indicate an OSPF neighbor adjacency problem. Commands such as ping and traceroute, followed by routing table and forwarding checks, are more appropriate for locating that failure.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of ports in RSTP offer routes to the root switch? (Choose two.)

Root Port (RP): Connects upstream to root switch or upstream switch; one per switch.
Designated Port (DP): Receives and forwards frames to other switches and connects to downstream devices; one per link.
Alternate Port: Provides an alternate route to the root switch via a different switch.
Backup Port: Offers link redundancy toward a shared segment within a single collision domain, usually a network hub.

questions.stem: Which tool can be used to ensure that a service provider is meeting its guaranteed metrics for customers?

questions.stem: Which of the following performs a one-to-one, permanent mapping of an organization's private IP addresses to public IP addresses? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
The three main types of Network Address Translation (NAT) include:

Static NAT: A private address has a static one-to-one mapping to a public address. Static NAT is further broken up into inside and outside static NAT. Inside static NAT conceals an organization's private IP addresses, while outside static NAT conceals the IP addresses of a remote system.
Pooled NAT: Local Internet Protocol (IP) addresses are dynamically assigned one-to-one to a public address, which returns to the pool after a period of disuse.
Port Address Translation (PAT): Many local IP addresses are mapped to a single public IP address. Each internal IP/port combination in use is mapped to a different port on the public IP address.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of hypervisors needs a host OS?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Type 2

A hypervisor is software that allows multiple Virtual Machines (VMs) to run on the same hardware. There are two types of hypervisors:

Type 1: A Type I, bare-metal, or native hypervisor runs directly on the device hardware with no Operating System (OS). Examples of Type 1 hypervisors include VMware vSphere, Citrix Hypervisor, and Red Hat Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM).
Type 2: Type 2 hypervisors are software that runs within a host OS. VirtualBox and VMware Fusion are examples of Type 2 hypervisors, which are typically used by client machines.

There are no Type 0 or Type 3 hypervisors.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the first of the BGP neighbor states?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Idle

The Border Gateway Protocol ( BGP) defines six neighbor states, including:

Idle: Initial state of the BGP Finite State Machine (FSM), where the router sends Transport Control Protocol (TCP) connection requests and listens for connection requests from peers. If reentered due to error, resets ConnectRetryTimer to 60 and waits until it reaches 0 before trying again. Further failures cause the timer to double.
Connect: Router initiates the TCP three-way handshake. If successful, sends an Open message to a neighbor, resets ConnectRetryTimer, and transitions to OpenSent. If ConnectRetryTimer expires, attempts a new TCP connection and will transition to Active if the connection fails or Idle if other errors occur.
Active: Starts a new three-way TCP handshake. If successful, sends an Open message, sets hold timer to four minutes, and moves to OpenSent. If fails, reverts to Connect and resets ConnectRetryTimer.
OpenSent: Originating router waiting for an Open message from receiving router. Once received, Open messages are checked for any errors. If no errors, hold time is negotiated, KEEPALIVE is sent, and moves to OpenConfirm. Errors cause a NOTIFICATION message and reversion to Idle state. TCP disconnect causes closed connection, reset ConnectRetryTimer, and move to Active. Other events cause reversion to Idle.
OpenConfirm: Router waits for KEEPALIVE or NOTIFICATION. If KEEPALIVE receives, moves to Established. If an error occurs ( hold timer expiration, stop event, or received NOTIFICATION message), it reverts to Idle.
Established: BGP session established and neighbors exchange routes via UPDATE messages. UPDATEs and KEEPALIVES cause hold timer resets, and hold timer expiration causes error and reversion to Idle.

questions.stem: You need to capture packets from a local switch for analysis. Which command defines the source ports that will be used?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: monitor session 1 source interface gi1/0/1 - 4

This command explicitly defines the physical interfaces whose traffic will be mirrored for analysis. SPAN requires source interfaces to be configured, so the switch knows which traffic to copy.

The show monitor session local command is a verification command that displays configuration status rather than defining sources.

The monitor session 1 source vlan 10 mirrors VLAN traffic instead of specific physical interfaces.

The monitor session 1 direction ingress sets traffic direction but does not identify source ports.

questions.stem: Which HTTP status code occurs when the failure was related to a client-side issue?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: 400 Bad Request

The 400 Bad Request status code serves as the generic indicator that the server cannot process the request due to a perceived client error. It covers issues such as malformed request syntax and invalid request message framing.

200 OK is a success code indicating the request transitioned perfectly without any issues.

201 Created signifies that the request was successful and resulted in generation of the new resource on the server.

403 Forbidden means the server understood the request but refuses to authorize it.

questions.stem: Which of the following routing protocols generate a complete network map before selecting routes? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
Link state algorithms like Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) and Intermediate System-to-Intermediate System (IS-IS) advertise link states and metrics for all connected links and directly-connected routers to the entire network. With a complete map of the network, routers use Dijkstra’s Shortest Path First (SPF) algorithm to identify the best path to various destinations.

Distance vector routing protocols, such as the Routing Information Protocol version two (RIPv2), use vectors to specify the Internet Protocol (IP) address of the next hop to reach the destination. The distance can be measured as hop count and is the metric for choosing a route.

Enhanced distance vector algorithms like the Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL) used by the Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) can incorporate other metrics, such as bandwidth, reliability, delay, and load. It is also more efficient and allows traffic balancing across multiple routes.

Enhanced distance vector algorithms like the Diffusing Update Algorithm (DUAL) used by the Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) can incorporate other metrics, such as bandwidth, reliability, delay, and load. It is also more efficient and allows traffic balancing across multiple routes.

questions.stem: Which of the following involves temporary one-to-one assignments of IP addresses?

Static NAT: A private address has a static one-to-one mapping to a public address. Static NAT is further broken up into inside and outside static NAT.
Pooled NAT: Local Internet Protocol (IP) addresses are dynamically assigned one-to-one to a public address, which returns to the pool after a period of disuse.
Port Address Translation (PAT): Many local IP addresses are mapped to a single public IP address. Each internal IP/port combination in use is mapped to a different port on the public IP address.

questions.stem: Which of the following is not one of the key components of Cisco’s Locator/ID Separation Protocol (LISP)?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Management Plane

Cisco’s Locator/ID Separation Protocol (LISP) doesn't have a management plane. It has three main components:

LISP Routing Architecture: Traditionally, an IP address identifies a particular device at a specific location. LISP breaks it into separate Endpoint Identifiers (EIDs) and Routing Locators (RLOCs). If a device changes location, its EID stays the same while its RLOC changes.
LISP Control Plane: LISP converts EIDs to RLOCs by making a map request to the Map Resolver (MR). This pull-based model is more efficient than Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) or Open Shortest Path First (OSPF), which pushes route data, even for unused routes.
LISP Data Plane: An IP packet received from an EID is encapsulated in an Internet Protocol (IP)/User Datagram Protocol (UDP) packet using an IP address in the RLOC IP space.

questions.stem: A network engineer logs into a router but cannot run certain commands. Which command should they run to verify the set of commands available to them?

questions.stem: What are some profiling rules that Cisco AI Endpoint Analytics uses when determining priority of execution? (Choose three.)

options.text: Auto-generated rules through the Smart Grouping workflow

questions.explanation:
Cisco AI Endpoint Analytics uses multiple rule sources to prioritize endpoint profiling. Administrator-created static profiles allow a network engineer to manually define a device based on specific attributes, and these always take the highest priority to ensure human intent is followed. Default Cisco-provided system rules are built into the platform and use a massive database of known device fingerprints to automatically identify thousands of common hardware models. Auto-generated rules through the Smart Grouping workflow use machine learning to cluster similar unknown devices together and suggest a new rule that the administrator can then approve for the entire network.

Although vendors provide data, they do not create the internal AI profiling rules.

While NetFlow provides the data used by the rules, the devices themselves do not produce or define the profiling rules used by the AI engine.

Default Cisco-provided system rules are built into the platform and use a massive database of known device fingerprints to automatically identify thousands of common hardware models. Auto-generated rules through the Smart Grouping workflow use machine learning to cluster similar unknown devices together and suggest a new rule that the administrator can then approve for the entire network.

Although vendors provide data, they do not create the internal AI profiling rules.

Orchestration: SD-WAN Validator (previously vBond) implements the orchestration plane and performs tasks such as authentication, Network Address Translation (NAT) detection, and load balancing.
Control: The control plane is implemented using SD-WAN Controller (previously vSmart), which is responsible for defining the network topology and advertising routes and data policies to SD-WAN Edge devices.
Data: These SD-WAN Edge devices make up the data plane and are responsible for forwarding traffic between locations via various media.
Management: Cisco’s SD-WAN Manager Network Management System (NMS) implements the management plane, providing single-pane-of-glass visibility and control.

SD-WAN Analytics (previously vAnalytics) is an optional analytics service.

questions.stem: Which technology allows a single pNIC to map to a single VNF?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: PCI passthrough

PCI passthrough allows the hypervisor to step aside and map a physical PCI device, such as a high-speed network card, directly to a single virtual network function ( VNF). This means the VNF handles its own drivers and talks directly to the device, bypassing the software layers that usually slow things down.

Virtual switching is a shared model in which a software switch sits between the physical card and many different virtual machines, adding a minor delay.

A hypervisor is the broad management layer that runs the virtual machines, but it is the platform itself rather than the technology that maps the card to the VNF.

The VLAN Trunking Protocol (VTP) is used for managing VLANs on switches and doesn't relate to hardware virtualization.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a system that allows synchronization of router configuration and other data between redundant components on a router?
questions.explanation:

An RP is responsible for the routing table or Routing Information Base ( RIB), control plane, and (in centralized forwarding architectures) the adjacency table and Forwarding Information Base ( FIB).

questions.stem: An enterprise network uses the IntServ model to provide QoS for a mission-critical application. Arrange the following events in the order required to establish an end-to-end, per-flow resource reservation.

options.text: Each node along the path performs admission control as it processes the RESV message, verifying it has sufficient available resources to support the requested reservation
If admission control succeeds at every hop, each node reserves the requested bandwidth for that specific flow, completing the end-to-end reservation
The receiver sends an RSVP RESV message back along the reverse path, formally requesting the specific reservation needed for that flow
The transmitting host sends an RSVP PATH message that travels toward the destination, conveying traffic characteristics and establishing path state information at each intermediate router

questions.explanation:

The transmitting host sends an RSVP PATH message that travels toward the destination, conveying traffic characteristics and establishing path state information at each intermediate router: The sender initiates the process by advertising the flow characteristics and establishing the forward path state.
The receiver sends an RSVP RESV message back along the reverse path, formally requesting the specific reservation needed for that flow: The receiver initiates the actual resource request by sending a reservation upstream.
Each node along the path performs admission control as it processes the RESV message, verifying it has sufficient available resources to support the requested reservation: Routers determine whether the requested QoS guarantees can be honored before committing resources.
If admission control succeeds at every hop, each node reserves the requested bandwidth for that specific flow, completing the end-to-end reservation: Successful admission control results in a per-flow reservation being established across the entire path.

questions.stem: According to 802.1Q, what are the two 2-byte fields added to an Ethernet frame for Layer 2 marking? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
When an Ethernet frame is tagged, an 802.1Q header is inserted between the Source Address and the Type/Length fields. The first 2-byte part is the Tag Protocol Identifier (TPID), which is always set to the hex value 0x8100 to tell the receiving switch that this is a tagged frame. The second 2-byte part is the Tag Control Information (TCI), which contains the 3-bit priority value for QoS and the 12-bit VLAN ID.

The Start Frame Delimiter (SFD) is a 1-byte field that marks the end of the preamble and the beginning of the actual frame.

The Frame Check Sequence (FCS) is a 4-byte trailer used for error detection at the very end of the frame.

questions.stem: Which of the following solutions are designed to protect against forwarding loops caused by a broken strand in a fiber-optic cable? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
With fiber, a link may only work in one direction but appear up if a strand is broken. Eventually, the downstream port may discover that its root port doesn’t work and switch to an alternate root port. This creates a forwarding loop if traffic received on the new root port is forwarded out of the functional strand in the old root port.

This is addressed via a few solutions:

STP Loop Guard: Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) loop guard prevents alternative or root ports from becoming designated ports if the root port stops receiving Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs). The original root is placed in a loop inconsistent state while down and can recover and transition through STP states after the issue is fixed. Loop guard is enabled globally with spanning-tree loopguard default or locally with spanning-tree guard loop. It shouldn’t be used on portfast-enabled ports.
Unidirectional Link Detection (UDLD): UDLD monitors fiber-optic cables in both directions by sending UDLD packets over them that include the system ID and port ID of the sender, and the recipient replies with a similar packet. In normal mode, unacknowledged frames cause the link to be undetermined and remain active. In aggressive mode, a missed frame causes the sender to send eight more packets in one-second intervals and place the port in an error state if these are not acknowledged either. UDLD is enabled globally with udld enable [aggressive] and locally enabled with udld port [aggressive] or disabled with udld port disable. The udld recovery [interval time] command allows recovery with an optional user-defined interval (default five minutes).

Portfast and root guard protect against other potential causes of Layer 2 loops.

questions.stem:
A retailer has 120 branch stores and needs to securely connect each site to multiple cloud applications while ensuring consistent performance, centralized policy control, and rapid onboarding of new locations. WAN circuits vary by region, and outages frequently disrupt operations.

A 3-tier enterprise network design applies to a campus LAN architecture, not WAN or cloud connectivity.

A controller-less WLAN addresses wireless access design rather than inter-site or cloud WAN connectivity.

A site-to-site IPsec VPN does not scale as well and lacks centralized policy control.

questions.stem: In LISP routing architecture, what changes when an endpoint roams from site to site?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: RLOC

In a LISP architecture, the Endpoint Identifier (EID) is the name or permanent IP address of the device. It never changes, which allows active sessions like a video call or a file transfer to continue without dropping. When an endpoint roams to a new site, the new router (ITR/ETR) notifies the map server (MS) that the specific EID is now reachable through its own RLOC.

The purpose of LISP is to ensure the EID remains constant regardless of where the device moves in the network.

The LISP protocol itself is focused on the Layer 3 separation of identity and location rather than on hardware MAC addresses.

LISP presents a distributed or anycast gateway experience to the endpoint.

questions.stem: In a Cisco router, where is routing information stored? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
The Routing Information Base (RIB) is Cisco’s term for a routing table, which stores information abouthow to reach different devices or networks.

The Forwarding Information Base (FIB) stores the next-hop information for each network destination and is used to make Internet Protocol (IP) destination prefix-based decisions about how to route packets.

An adjacency table or the Adjacency Information Base (AIB), which is part of software CEF, contains the next-hop Media Access Control (MAC) addresses for each directly connected next-hop IP address as well as the MAC address of the egress interface. It’s populated by the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) or similar sources.

Content Addressable Memory (CAM) holds the MAC address table and uses specialized search techniques to enable addresses to be found faster than with Random Access Memory (RAM).

Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM) is memory on a Cisco switch that allows multiple different fields to be used to evaluate a packet. It’s used for Layer 2 or 3 searching and returns 0, 1, or X (don’t care).

questions.stem: What does using the Multicast Source Discovery Protocol (MSDP) enable?

options.text: Replacing IGMP with host-to-router multicast signaling

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Connecting multiple PIM sparse-mode domains

MSDP allows rendezvous points in different administrative regions to share information about active multicast sources so that traffic can flow between them. This protocol is essential for any-source multicast when a receiver in one domain needs to find a source located in a completely different domain.

First-hop redundancy protocols such as HSRP and VRRP are used for gateway availability, so they are unrelated to multicast source discovery.

IGMP is the protocol used for communication between hosts and their local routers and is not replaced by the inter-domain functions of MSDP.

MSDP is a control plane protocol that advertises source information and does not provide any native encryption or data protection features.

questions.stem: Which solution allows for mirroring packets at the data plane level to assist in troubleshooting?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: SPAN

Switch Port Analyzer (SPAN) is the solution that allows you to copy traffic from a source port (or VLAN) and send it to a destination port where a monitoring device is connected. Because this happens at the data plane level, you get a bit-for-bit duplicate of the original packets, including headers and payloads.

IP Service Level Agreements (IPSLA) are used to generate synthetic traffic to measure network performance rather than mirroring existing packets for analysis.

NetFlow provides statistics about traffic patterns, but it records only the metadata of the conversation rather than mirroring the actual packets themselves.

The Simple Network Management Protocol ( SNMP) is used for managing devices rather than capturing packet data.

questions.stem: In YANG, which of the following node types is used to create subtrees?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: Container

The Yet Another Next Generation ( YANG) data model language defines four types of nodes:

Leaf Node: Leaf nodes contain a single value of a particular type and have no children.
Leaf-List Node: Leaf-list nodes are sequences of leaf nodes with a single value of a particular type for each leaf node.
Container Node: Container nodes collect multiple related nodes into a subtree. Container nodes have child nodes but no value and contain an unlimited number of child nodes of any type.
List Node: List nodes hold a series of list entries, which act as records and are identified by their key leaves. A list node can have multiple keys and an unlimited number of child nodes of any type.

questions.stem: Place the following functions of a traditional hierarchical campus architecture in their logical sequence, beginning with the layer closest to end-user devices and progressing toward core transport and enterprise edge connectivity.

options.text: Implement high-availability mechanisms, and optimize routing through summarization and policy controls
Extend connectivity to data-center resources, internet services, and external WAN destinations
Deliver resilient, high-speed transport between major campus domains and enterprise services
Consolidate multiple access-layer segments, and perform Layer 3 forwarding between VLANs
Establish physical and logical connectivity for user systems, wireless access points, and other edge devices

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

Establish physical and logical connectivity for user systems, wireless access points, and other edge devices: This defines the complete operational scope of the Access Layer, where corporate assets physically hit the wire and receive initial security profiles.
Consolidate multiple access-layer segments, and perform Layer 3 forwarding between VLANs: This marks the physical and logical transition into the Distribution Layer, where edge links are aggregated, and local traffic is routed.
Implement high-availability mechanisms, and optimize routing through summarization and policy controls: This represents the advanced control-plane functions of the Distribution Layer, isolating local topology instability from the network backbone.
Deliver resilient, high-speed transport between major campus domains and enterprise services: The Core Layer's main purpose is to deliver uncompromised, rapid packet switching with zero policy overhead.
Extend connectivity to data-center resources, internet services, and external WAN destinations: This represents the absolute egress vector, leaving the campus core to interface with edge blocks and external service providers.

questions.stem: How does a switch configured with an RSPAN VLAN differ from a standard Layer 2 switch? (Choose two.)

options.text: MAC addresses are not learned on ports associated with the RSPAN VLAN
Ports in the RSPAN VLAN should ignore the spanning tree state
Traffic is flooded out all ports associated with the RSPAN VLAN
The RSPAN VLAN must be configured as the native VLAN on all trunks

questions.explanation:
An RSPAN VLAN differs from a typical VLAN because it is optimized to transport mirrored traffic without the overhead or logic of traditional bridging. RSPAN VLANs flood mirrored traffic so that it can traverse the network and reach the remote destination switch without relying on MAC learning. MAC address learning is disabled on RSPAN VLANs to prevent mirrored traffic from polluting the CAM table.

The Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) still applies to RSPAN VLANs to prevent Layer 2 loops.

The RSPAN VLAN is simply allowed on trunks and does not require native VLAN status.

questions.stem: Which Cisco solution uses the Overlay Management Protocol (OMP) to learn and disseminate routing information?
questions.explanation:

Cisco’s Catalyst Software-Defined Wide Area Network (SD-WAN) solution implements four planes:

Control: The control plane is implemented using SD-WAN Controller (formerly vSmart), which is responsible for defining the network topology and uses the Overlay Management Protocol (OMP) to advertise routes to SD-WAN Edge devices.
Management: Cisco’s SD-WAN Manager Network Management System (NMS) implements the management plane, providing single-pane-of-glass visibility and control.
Orchestration: SD-WAN Validator (formerly vBond) implements the orchestration plane and performs tasks such as authentication, Network Address Translation (NAT) detection, and load balancing.
Data: These SD-WAN Edge devices make up the data plane and are responsible for forwarding traffic between locations via various media.

SD-WAN Analytics (formerly vAnalytics) is an optional analytics service.

questions.stem: Which of the following routing protocols is capable of load balancing traffic over multiple paths with unequal costs?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: EIGRP

Unequal-cost load balancing is a non-default option available in the Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP) where multiple routes with different path metrics are included in the routing table. Traffic is load-balanced in ratios based on the relative path metrics.

Equal-Cost Multipathing (ECMP) allows multiple different routes to be included in a routing table if they are equally good. Traffic is load-balanced across all of these routes, increasing available bandwidth. Routing Information Protocol version two (RIPv2), Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP), Open Shortest Path First (OSPF), and Intermediate System-to-Intermediate System (IS-IS) can all use ECMP.

Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is an exterior gateway protocol, unlike the others.

questions.stem: You applied a CoPP policy but need to confirm that it is actually active and policing traffic. Which command should you use?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: show policy-map control-plane input

The show policy-map control-plane input command displays the policy map applied to the control plane along with class statistics and counters. This output confirms both that the CoPP policy is attached, and that traffic is being matched and policed.

The show running-config command only shows configuration statements, so it does not confirm operational policy attachment or traffic counters.

The show ip access-lists control-plane command displays the entries of an access list but does not show the rate limiting behavior of a policy map.

The show policy-map control-plane output command is incorrect since CoPP only supports input direction policies, not output.

questions.stem: Which of the following types of BGP messages can be used to reset the hold timer? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
The Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) uses four message types, including:

KEEPALIVE: Verifies connectivity to BGP neighbors. Sent every 1/3 of hold time, defaulting to every 60 seconds on Cisco routers. Received KEEPALIVE resets the hold timer.
UPDATE: Sends changes to BGP routes, including advertisements, updates, or withdrawals. Can also act as a KEEPALIVE, resetting the hold timer.
OPEN: Creates and establishes BGP adjacency. Defines the hold time, BGP Router ID (RID), and other parameters for the session.
NOTIFICATION: Notifies a BGP neighbor of an error condition, such as an expired hold timer, changing capabilities, or requested BGP session reset, and closes the BGP connection.

UPDATE: Sends changes to BGP routes, including advertisements, updates, or withdrawals. Can also act as a KEEPALIVE, resetting the hold timer.
OPEN: Creates and establishes BGP adjacency. Defines the hold time, BGP Router ID (RID), and other parameters for the session.
NOTIFICATION: Notifies a BGP neighbor of an error condition, such as an expired hold timer, changing capabilities, or requested BGP session reset, and closes the BGP connection.

questions.stem: Where on a Cisco switch is stored information about how to reach different networks and devices?
questions.explanation:
Correct answer: RIB

The Routing Information Base (RIB) is Cisco’s term for a routing table, which stores information about how to reach different devices or networks.

Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM) is memory on a Cisco switch that allows multiple different fields to be used to evaluate a packet. It’s used for Layer 2 and 3 searching and returns 0, 1, or X (don’t care).

The Forwarding Information Base (FIB) stores the next-hop information for each network destination and is used to make Internet Protocol (IP) destination prefix-based decisions about how to route packets.

An adjacency table or the Adjacency Information Base (AIB), which is part of software CEF, contains the next-hop MAC addresses for each directly connected next-hop IP address as well as the Media Access Control (MAC) address of the egress interface. It’s populated by the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) table or similar sources.

questions.stem: Where does an internal spanning tree ( IST) run when using MST?

options.text: Only in specific VLANs on switch port interfaces in an MST region
On every switch port interface in the MST region
Only on the root bridge of the region
On all trunk port interfaces in VLAN0

questions.explanation:
Correct answer: On every switch port interface in the MST region

The IST is a special instance that runs on every physical port within an MST region, regardless of which VLANs are assigned to those ports. It is responsible for building the common spanning tree topology that connects all the switches in the region together and handles communication with any external switches running traditional STP or Rapid-STP.

IST is a foundational instance that operates across the physical infrastructure to support all VLANs rather than being restricted to a few.

VLAN0 is not a standard usable VLAN in Cisco networking.

Every switch in the region must participate in the IST to exchange information, not just the root bridge.

questions.stem: A network engineer is troubleshooting a branch router. They notice that the router is rewriting the address of an external server before presenting it to an internal host. Which NAT term describes this address?

Inside local refers to the private IP address of an inside host before translation.

Outside global represents the real, globally routable IP address of the outside host.

Inside global is the translated public IP address representing an inside host to the outside network.

questions.stem: Which of the following are Cisco-proprietary protocols for deploying redundant network gateways? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation:
First-Hop Redundancy Protocols (FHRP) help ensure network resiliency by creating a Virtual Internet Protocol (VIP) gateway linked to multiple physical gateways. If a gateway goes down, then the device’s traffic will be sent via another gateway. The three main FHRPs include:

Hot Standby Router Protocol (HSRP): Protocol developed by Cisco that creates a virtual IP and Media Access Control (MAC) address usually held by the active router. If the active router fails, a standby router takes over these addresses and acts as the gateway.
Gateway Load Balancing Protocol (GLBP): Cisco-proprietary protocol that offers both redundancy and load balancing. The network has up to four Active Virtual Forwarders (AVFs) responsible for forwarding traffic for their assigned hosts and a single Active Virtual Gateway (AVG) that responds to Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) requests with the virtual MAC of the assigned AVF. Failure of the AVG or an AVF causes another system to take over its role.
Virtual Router Redundancy Protocol (VRRP): Industry standard protocol that operates similarly to HSRP but names the routers “master” and “backup”. This protocol allows preemption by default and uses a particular MAC address structure for the VIP gateway.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements accurately describe shared trees when using PIM? (Choose two.)

options.text: The root of the tree is a router referred to as the Rendezvous Point (RP)
They require more multicast entries compared to using source trees
They provide the most optimal path for every individual source
The receiver receives traffic from all sources sending traffic to the same multicast group

questions.explanation:
In a shared tree with Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM), all multicast traffic is initially routed through a central Rendezvous Point (RP) that serves as the root of the tree. Receivers join the shared tree for a multicast group and can receive traffic from multiple active sources through that same tree. This design simplifies multicast state by aggregating sources under a single distribution structure.

Shared trees reduce state by maintaining group-based entries rather than per source entries.

Traffic may take suboptimal paths through the RP rather than the shortest path routes.

questions.stem: Order the following steps describing how Cisco Catalyst Center's Controller Layer works with Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) to make and apply a group-based policy decision within an SD-Access fabric.

options.text: Catalyst Center synchronizes Scalable Groups and contracts with ISE via an API
Catalyst Center pushes SGACL policy down to fabric edge/border nodes
The ISE authenticates and returns authorization and SGT assignment
An endpoint connects, and an edge node sends authentication credentials to the ISE (AAA)
Fabric nodes enforce SGACLs based on source/destination SGTs in the VXLAN header
An administrator defines a group‑based access control policy in Catalyst Center

questions.explanation:
Correct answer order:

An administrator defines a group‑based access control policy in Catalyst Center: Policy intent must be established before identities and enforcement mechanisms can use it.
Catalyst Center synchronizes Scalable Groups and contracts with ISE via an API: The management and policy systems must share a common policy model prior to endpoint onboarding.
An endpoint connects, and an edge node sends authentication credentials to the ISE ( AAA): The endpoint must be authenticated so that an identity-based policy decision can be made.
The ISE authenticates and returns authorization and SGT assignment: The ISE classifies the endpoint and assigns the identity context that will drive policy enforcement.
Catalyst Center pushes SGACL policy down to fabric edge/border nodes: The fabric infrastructure receives the policies necessary to enforce the centrally defined communication rules.
Fabric nodes enforce SGACLs based on source/destination SGTs in the VXLAN header: The data plane applies identity-based access controls as traffic traverses the SD-Access fabric.

questions.stem: Which component in LISP architecture de-encapsulates LISP-encapulated IP packets coming from sites outside the LISP site?
questions.explanation:

These packets are encapsulated by the ITR at the source site and delivered to the destination site’s Egress Tunnel Router (ETR). The ETR removes the outer header and forwards the original packet to the endpoint.

ITRs encapsulate traffic leaving a LISP site, not traffic entering it.

EIDs are addresses used for identification, not forwarding devices.

questions.stem: Which of the following steps are involved when configuring inside static NAT? (Choose two.)

questions.stem: Which of the following methods are considered best practices for implementing password protection on a line? (Choose two.)
